name: can-card

name: can-check

name: can-clean-up-mess
description: LLM-driven data preparation pipeline for cleaning, integrating, and enriching messy datasets. Use when the user says 'clean this data', 'fix this CSV', 'match these schemas', 'deduplicate these records', 'impute missing values', or 'annotate this table'.

name: can-communication

allowed_tools: Read, Write, Glob, Grep, Edit, WebFetch, WebSearch, Bash

name: can-complete-goal
description: Check whether the goal can be completed based on current acceptance criteria. Blocks on self-claimed required criteria.

name: can-debug
description: 当需要调试 CAN 总线通信时使用，支持通过 USB-CAN 适配器监听、发送 CAN 帧和扫描节点。

name: can-decode
description: Check if a video can be decoded by the browser using Mediabunny

name: can-do
description: Use for autonomous task delivery across models and agent environments: complete the requested work, resolve routine uncertainty, recover from failures and verify the result without needless questions.

name: can-do-statement-writer
description: Write and review can-do statements for language courses, units, lessons and learner self-assessment, CEFR or NCSSFL-ACTFL style: action (observable verb) + text or situation + level-specific conditions, learner ('I can') and descriptor ('Can') versions, progressions of one activity from A1 to C1, and coverage of reception, production, interaction and mediation. Includes a verb bank by mode and level and condition and text-type banks. Lints statements for teacher-centred phrasing, knowledge instead of use (learn, know, understand the passive), missing context, two skills in one statement, vagu…

name: can-error-analysis
description: Root-cause analysis of CAN error frames (TxErr/RxErr) from the CANoe Protocol Monitor. Use for missampling, sample-point/bit-timing issues, or cross-network error correlation. Explains how to correctly interpret error position and BRS/ESI/DLC flag validity.

name: can-finn-eat-here-skill
description: Determine whether Finn can eat a satisfactory meal at a named restaurant and location by researching current menus, restaurant statements, HappyCow, ordering platforms, and other public evidence. Use when asked whether a restaurant, cafe, takeaway, food venue, or particular branch is suitable for Finn's vegan diet, peanut and pecan intolerance, and avoidance of canola or rapeseed oil.

name: can-free
description: 基于时钟地址命名协议，对内容加盖时间戳与哈希，本地三列日志记录与自评估。Use when 需要系统监控、日志分析、运维告警、部署管理时使用。不适用于物理硬件维修。适用于独立开发者、企业团队和自动化工作流场景。支持中文交互，无需复杂配置即开即用。输出结果可直接使用，减少二次加工成本。提供结构化输出和错误处理机制。

name: can-hunt
description: Совместный поиск сигналов в CAN-шине машины вместе с пользователем, который сидит в машине у ноутбука. Claude смотрит поток CAN с контроллера UniversalController (G4/H723/H503, прошивка со сниффером) через монитор UC_<плата>_Monitor.exe, даёт пошаговые инструкции на странице /assist, анализирует записи и находит поле. Применять, когда пользователь хочет найти данные в CAN машины — обороты, скорость, педали газа и тормоза, селектор PRND, ручник, руль, поворотники, свет, двери, замки, кнопки на руле, ключ, температуру, топливо, скорости колёс; говорит «подключись к машине», «поехали, ищем оборо…

name: can-i-actually-rank
description: Check whether a candidate keyword is actually winnable by reading the live SERP, then apply five commercial filters. Ends every candidate in QUALIFY, CONDITIONAL or KILL, kills freely, and never treats vendor authority scores as evidence. Use this skill whenever the user asks to: - Check whether they can rank for a keyword before building content - Qualify or kill a list of keyword candidates - Understand what format Google actually rewards for a query - Decide whether a topic is worth the effort Trigger even for casual requests like "can we rank for this", "check the SERPs for these keywords…

name: can-i-add-x
description: Use this when a homeowner asks "can I add a hot tub / heat pump / induction range / generator / EV charger / sauna?" Gives a planning-level headroom framing from their saved panel profile and ends with what a licensed electrician and the AHJ will check. EV asks hand off to chargeright-ev.

name: can-i-afford-it
description: Use this skill when the user asks whether a purchase or a change fits their money — a big buy, a trip, a new monthly cost, a pay cut, losing their job, how long their cash would last. Use it for 'can I afford X', 'should I wait on the car', 'how many months of runway do I have', even when no price is given yet. Not for progress toward savings goals or retirement (on-track), not for which investment to buy, not for setting budget targets (budget-review).

name: can-i-afford-this
description: Works out a what if in Agentic Money View without touching the real figures: builds a scenario (a van at £450 a month, a hire at £2,400 a month from March, losing Greenway Café), switches it on, and explains what the What if view then shows, with a one-paragraph note. The numbers come from the app, never from Claude. Use when the app asks (an Ask Claude question on What if), or when they say "can I afford a van?", "what if I hire someone?", "what if I lose Greenway?", "what happens if I take a month off?" or "can I afford a pay rise?".

name: can-i-buy
description: Whether something fits this month's plan in Wonderful. A want is checked against guilt-free money left after bills, a need against all spending left after bills.

name: can-i-delete-this
description: Use when the user asks whether some code can be deleted, why a line or block exists, or who introduced it, especially in a repository whose history is too large to read directly or when `git blame` returned a formatting or refactoring commit instead of a real answer. Traces the true introducing commit through formatter noise, renames, code moves and squashed history, then grades deletion risk with commit-level evidence. Triggers include "can I delete this", "why is this here", "what is this code for", "이 코드 지워도 되나", "이거 왜 있는 거지", "누가 넣었지".

name: can-i-go
description: Helps students keep a life outside class by finishing every Canvas assignment a day before it's due, so the answer to "can I go?" is yes. Use when a student asks if they can go out or sends a party, game or trip invite, asks what to do first, how long work will take or how busy the week looks, sends a work schedule photo, wants new Canvas assignments flagged, or says they keep leaving work to the last minute. Unlike a one-off study plan, it sets a finish-by date a day before each deadline, ranks work by time left, checks Canvas daily for new work, submissions and grades, follows up after ever…

name: can-i-help
description: Use when the user asks "where to help", "contribution opportunities", or "find a good first issue". Returns data-backed first steps. Not for PR review queues: use gh-review-requests.

name: can-i-merge
description: Use when asking whether a pull request is finished — "can we merge", "can i merge", "is this PR ready", "is it done", "ship check" — or before asking anyone to review or approve one. Also use before calling a ticket complete because its PR is green, and before reporting that a change is verified.

name: can-i-play-it-on-zeldas-ocarina
description: Use when someone asks whether a song or melody can be played on Link's ocarina in Ocarina of Time (Switch 2 remake), pastes notes to play, or wants the button inputs to play it in-game.

name: can-i-publish
description: 使用 can-i-publish CLI 检查 npm 包名、组织名及 scoped 包名的可用性，识别占用和相似度限制，并查找替代名称。当用户需要选择或验证 npm 名称、批量检查候选名或排查包名相似度阻止时使用。

name: can-i-self-host-composio-on-my-own-vm-73c7774f5537cdfa
description: Shows how to fix can I self host Composio on my own VM?. Use it when you hit this exact problem. Skip it when your error message or symptom looks different.

name: can-i-take-this
description: Check whether a GitHub issue is free to work on before anyone starts. Use when the user shares a GitHub issue and asks whether they can take, claim or start it, or whether someone is already working on it, and before you begin work on any GitHub issue yourself, so nobody opens a duplicate pull request.

name: can-i-use
description: Check browser support for web platform features (CSS, JS APIs, HTML) against the project's actual browser targets. Resolves the project's browserslist config, queries caniuse/MDN compatibility data, reports Baseline status, and recommends fallbacks or progressive enhancement. Use when asking "can I use X", choosing between modern and legacy approaches, reviewing code for unsupported features, or auditing browser compatibility.

name: can-i-use-check
description: checks if a CSS, JavaScript, HTML or Web-API -feature compatibility via https://caniuse.com

name: can-implement-agent-based-odd-based
description: Translate ODD protocol specifications into validated, executable agent-based model (ABM) code in Python. Use when the user says 'implement this ABM', 'convert ODD to code', 'build an agent-based model from this specification', 'replicate this NetLogo model in Python', 'translate this model description into a simulation', or 'create a predator-prey / ecological / social ABM'.

name: can-induced-emotion-bias-llm-behaviors-in-sequenti
description: Can Induced Emotion Bias LLM Behaviors in Sequential Decision Making? - As Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in high-stakes domains, understanding contextual factors that may modul...

name: can-it-run-doom
description: Judge whether a design generates capabilities from primitives or enumerates them one at a time. Not a complexity critic: the count of things is not the defect. Ask what happens when someone wants something nobody enumerated - do they compose what is already there, or must the design invent another answer. The finding is always a primitive that does not exist, never a thing to cut. Use on can it run doom, can it do X, is this general, is this overbuilt, is this a substrate, will this extend, why does every new feature need new code, what is this actually built on, before committing to a shape,…

name: can-jack-help
description: Answers "Can Jack help me with…?" questions about Jack Zorola, an operations leader (Chief of Staff / Director of Operations / PMO). Use whenever someone asks whether Jack could help with a problem, a role, a project or a skill, whether he is a fit for a job description, or what he has actually done in an area. Gives an honest verdict grounded only in the evidence in this file.

description: 向来访者简明解释认知行为疗法中事件、思维与情绪三者之间的因果关系，帮助其建立初步的元认知觉察框架。用于咨询初期建立治疗联盟和心理教育基础。

name: CBT技能归因与生活化迁移训练
description: 在咨询结束阶段，将来访者在咨询中习得并实践的CBT工具（如三栏表、箭头向下、双重故事）明确归因于其自身能动性与选择，并协同其识别72小时内可及的真实生活情境，设定微小、可验证的行为证据收集任务，以支持新核心信念（如‘我有我价值’‘我有能力’）的持续内化与行动化。

name: CBT放松训练：网络疑病相关自主神经调节
description: 在个案干预中段，针对网络疑病诱发的自主神经高唤醒状态，系统引导来访者习得并练习渐进式肌肉放松或腹式呼吸技术，并通过结构化家庭作业巩固技能；全程强调正常化、非评判觉察与个体化调适。

name: CBT暴露后恶性循环认知解构
description: 在单次现实暴露结束后，引导来访者识别并命名由回避行为维持的‘焦虑-厌恶-回避’自我强化循环，用具体事件链说明其如何阻断自然习惯化过程。

name: CBT核心信念四句锚定小结
description: 在单次CBT咨询结束阶段，以精炼、非说教、生活化方式陈述四句核心认知行为原理，用于强化概念内化、支持作业执行，并为后续干预建立共同理解框架。

name: CBT核心信念巩固性重述
description: 在巩固阶段，引导来访者用第一人称、现在时、肯定句式重述已修正的核心信念，强调接纳局限性与生活平衡价值，强化新认知的稳定性与自我归属感。

name: CBT核心信念探索与能力再评估工作流程
description: 通过回顾个人经历、行为实验与能力盘点，引导来访者接触并松动关于自我、他人、世界的深层核心信念，重点重建自我效能感，适用于咨询中后期寻求根本性认同转变的情境。

name: CBT核心信念温习微作业布置
description: 在CBT单次咨询结束阶段，向求助者布置每日5分钟温习本次共同构建的1–3条合理核心信念的家庭作业，以强化神经可塑性、促进信念内化与行为迁移；严格限定形式（默读/朗读/录音复听）、时长（固定5分钟）、频次（每日一次）、起始时间（当日即始），不附加反思或实验任务。

name: CBT核心信念矫正工作流程
description: 通过识别自动思维→追溯中间信念→挖掘核心信念→检验证据→发展替代性核心信念的标准化序列，系统性更新来访者关于自我、他人、世界的核心信念。适用于已建立稳定咨询关系、能耐受认知探索的情绪困扰来访者。

name: CBT核心信念识别与协同重构
description: 在咨询初期、信任关系已初步建立的前提下，运用CBT认知概念化框架识别求助者不合理核心信念，并通过苏格拉底式提问、证据检验与协作生成等方式，引导其发展更具现实性、适应性与弹性的替代信念。

name: CBT深呼吸放松训练
description: 引导来访者通过有节奏的深呼吸练习实现生理与心理同步放松，用于缓解急性焦虑、改善睡眠启动障碍。适用于咨询中或日常自我调节场景。

name: CBT渐进式意象放松引导
description: 在首次咨询中向来访者教授标准化渐进性放松训练步骤，指导其每日3分钟自主练习，并明确反馈要求，以快速缓解焦虑、改善睡眠及增强自我调节感。

name: CBT焦虑-羞愧情绪链识别微干预
description: 在第3–4次CBT咨询中，基于个案具体生理/行为线索（如手心出汗、回避检查），引导其即时识别羞愧、内疚、自责等特定情绪，并锚定其背后的自动化思维与中间信念，构建‘情境→情绪→思维→信念’的可命名、可复述的觉察链条。

name: CBT焦虑干预四阶段流程
description: 一个结构化、分阶段的CBT个案干预框架，适用于学习受挫引发的青少年焦虑问题，含评估、认知重构、行为练习与巩固四个阶段。

name: CBT现实暴露中的实时情绪锚定与反馈
description: 在可控现实暴露过程中，咨询师每3～5分钟主动询问来访者当前主观焦虑强度（0–10分），同步引导其觉察情绪峰值时刻的自动思维变化，并在暴露结束后即时联结情绪消退体验与认知修正（如‘所担心的事并未发生’），以强化情绪-认知联结学习。

name: CBT现实暴露任务分级与实施计划
description: 在认知行为疗法框架下，为焦虑相关人际情境设计等级化暴露任务，并协同来访者制定包含去灾难化、回避行为教育、目标设定三要素的暴露实施计划。

name: CBT社交恐惧症暴露练习结构化方案
description: 在认知行为疗法框架下，为社交恐怖症求助者设计并实施渐进式暴露练习的结构化会话流程，含情绪监控、情景分级、作业布置与反思要求。

name: CBT社交焦虑阶段性咨询框架
description: 一个结构化、分阶段的CBT咨询流程，覆盖从建立联盟、认知重构到行为暴露与复发预防的全过程，专用于社交焦虑障碍的系统干预。

name: CBT终期会谈结构化框架
description: 在认知行为疗法（CBT）第10次（终期）咨询中，系统性完成认知成果巩固、疗效评估、现实迁移预演与分离情绪处理的标准化会谈流程。

name: CBT结束阶段三重巩固协议
description: 在最后一次CBT咨询中同步执行三项核心任务：引导来访者回顾自身变化与已掌握的有效技术、协助处理分离焦虑、共同构建现实可行的复发预防策略，形成结构化、内化导向的闭环收尾。

name: CBT结束阶段再教育与技能泛化工作流程
description: 在CBT咨询末期，结构化回顾咨询历程，强化新习得的认知与行为技能，指导求助者将所学迁移至日常生活场景，尤其聚焦人际交往中的情绪调节与沟通技巧应用。

name: CBT结构化单次咨询流程
description: 在每次认知行为治疗会谈中，按固定顺序执行六个环节：当前状况与心境检查、与上次会谈的联结、议程设置、家庭作业回顾、议程议题讨论与新作业布置、阶段总结；确保会谈聚焦、高效且具教学性。

name: CBT考前焦虑三阶段咨询框架
description: 一个面向大学生考前焦虑的结构化CBT咨询流程，分为建立关系、心理帮扶（认知重构）、巩固应用三个阶段，每阶段有明确任务与方法指向，提供跨会话的阶段性CBT干预主干。

name: CBT考试焦虑三阶段咨询框架
description: 一个结构化、阶段化的认知行为疗法咨询流程，覆盖诊断评估与关系建立、心理帮助（含认知重构与放松训练）、结束与巩固三个核心阶段，适用于考试焦虑个案。

name: CBT考试焦虑三阶段咨询流程
description: 一个结构化、阶段化的认知行为疗法咨询流程，专用于医学生考试焦虑干预，覆盖关系建立与评估、认知重建与技能训练、效果巩固与结束三个阶段，共5次会谈。

name: CBT自动思维反驳话术模板
description: 提供一组结构化、可复用的自我反驳语句，用于挑战‘我不行’类核心负性自动思维，适用于咨询中引导来访者进行认知重构练习。

name: CBT自动思维识别与反应训练
description: 引导来访者使用标准认知工具识别并回应自动思维，以觉察功能不良认知和逻辑歪曲，从而减轻情绪症状。

name: CBT自动思维识别与苏格拉底式提问引导
description: 在认知行为疗法框架下，引导来访者识别特定情境中的负性自动思维，并通过结构化苏格拉底式提问促使其评估思维的真实性与适应性。适用于来访者已建立基本咨询关系、能报告具体情境与情绪反应时。

name: CBT自动思维识别与调整四步法
description: 在CBT会话中期干预阶段，引导来访者系统识别并挑战功能不良自动思维的结构化技术：①证据检验；②生成替代解释；③评估可能性（最坏/最好/最可能）；④自我同情提问。聚焦思维可塑性与认知弹性培养，强调协作性检验与来访者主动生成。

name: CBT自动思维识别与调整四步法
description: 在CBT框架下，使用结构化提问序列引导来访者从情绪出发，逐层挖掘自动化思维、中间信念与核心信念，实现认知内容的外化与层级标注。

name: CBT苏格拉底提问_不合理信念强度评估
description: 使用0–100%百分比量化技术，评估来访者对已明确定义的自动思维（如‘我很失败’）的主观确信度，作为认知重构的客观锚点；聚焦强度而非真假，要求整数输出与简要依据，闭环执行。

name: CBT行为实验设计与实施
description: 协同来访者设计可检验的假设性行为实验，用真实结果挑战适应不良信念，降低回避行为并提升情境自信。

name: CBT行为日志家庭作业布置与结构化反馈
description: 在首次咨询中标准化施测PHQ-9和GAD-7量表，向来访者解释结果含义，并据此形成初步工作评估，为CBT方案选择提供实证依据。

name: CBT认知修正引导框架
description: 一个聚焦于早期教育与意义重构的CBT会话支架，用于帮助来访者理解症状成因、识别自动化思维，并发展替代性叙述，尤其适用于道德颓废、罪恶感与羞耻相关困扰。

name: CBT认知偏差识别与重构引导
description: 在咨询中期阶段，引导来访者识别失恋和家庭关系中的不合理信念，并通过共同分析促发其认知调整动机。适用于来访者已建立基本咨访关系、情绪初步稳定、能配合叙述具体场景时。

name: CBT认知家庭作业结构化指派
description: 在来访者已理解ABC模型并完成至少一轮认知质辩后，指导其在生活情境中实践结构化认知重构：记录事件→识别自动思维→标注认知扭曲→生成合理替代想法→应用自我暗示，形成闭环练习。

name: CBT认知扭曲识别与面质
description: 在认知调整阶段，使用面质技术帮助来访者识别并挑战其'全或无'、'非黑即白'等极端化自动思维。适用于来访者已表达自我贬低（如'觉得自己是活该的'）且存在明显认知偏差时。

name: CBT认知概念化建模
description: 基于来访者信念与行为模式构建个体化认知概念化图，作为后续干预的理论锚点和治疗地图；用于每次咨询初始阶段或概念化修订时。

name: CBT认知行为干预阶段工作框架
description: 在心理咨询第3～8次中，系统性开展自动思维识别、正念觉察训练与行为激活三类核心干预，通过结构化家庭作业与会谈反馈形成闭环。适用于已建立基本咨访关系、情绪稳定性初步达标、有意愿配合结构化练习的来访者。

name: CBT认知重构双路径技术
description: 结合提问引导与自我审查两种互补策略：前者通过多角度提问揭示思维盲区，后者通过表达-体验-反省闭环促进不合理信念觉察与修正，聚焦舞台失误归因偏差。

name: CBT认知重构双路径技术
description: 一种短程认知干预模块，包含‘提问引导’（多角度提问促觉察不合理思维）与‘自我审查’（鼓励表达并反省自我看法）两个平行子路径，用于矫正舞台表现相关的错误归因与灾难化信念。

name: CBT认知重构四步工作法
description: 在心理帮助阶段（第2～5次）系统性地识别、检验、修正和巩固来访者错误认知的结构化会话级干预流程。适用于存在明显表层与核心错误观念、且情绪行为受其主导的来访者。

name: CBT认知重构引导流程
description: 在咨询中期阶段，通过分析来访者自我报告和测评结果，系统引导其识别并纠正与专业调剂相关的错误认知，促使其形成客观理性的现实评估。

name: CBT认知重构微干预：修正完美化投射认知偏差
description: 引导来访者识别、检验并替代关于偶像的绝对化、完美化自动思维，代之以基于努力、现实能力与具体领域的适应性信念；适用于来访者表达‘我永远比不上他’‘天生不如’等自我贬低式比较时。

name: CBT资源取向自我效能感激活技术
description: 在CBT咨询中段，系统引导个案回溯成长史中持续付出的努力与适应性应对策略，通过具象化叙事识别、命名并锚定其既有能力，削弱习得性无助认知，增强对生活的掌控感体验。

name: CBT适应性人际技能具身化辅导
description: 将抽象人际原则（如真诚、分享、不计较得失）转化为具体可操作的行为句式，通过 therapist 示范与来访者30秒内限时模拟，在低压力微情境中激活已有认知领悟，强化行为尝试动机与自我主张体验。

name: CBT阶段性认知-情绪-行为进展三方校验
description: 在咨询结束阶段，结构化核查抑郁情绪缓解、生活节律规律性、社会功能重建（如主动兼职）三项指标，结合来访者自述与咨询师观察，确认CBT干预已达临床稳定阈值，支持安全结案。

name: CBT非理性信念识别与辩论
description: 帮助来访者识别并修正对'威信'的单一化、极端化认知，通过多维度比较与自我评估，引导其建立更平衡、现实的自我评价框架。适用于来访者将威信等同于权威压制（如大吼大叫）并因此产生焦虑的情境。

name: CBT非理性信念识别与验证作业布置
description: 针对人际敏感类自动思维，引导来访者识别投射性认知偏差，布置行为实验性质的家庭作业以检验其真实性。

name: CBT非理性信念验证作业
description: 布置结构化家庭作业，引导求助者记录现实互动事件、自动思维及情绪反应，并设计简易验证行动（如主动询问、观察反证），用于检验投射性认知偏差。适用于已识别出具体非理性信念（如‘别人肯定不喜欢我’）且情绪稳定者。

name: CBT饼图时间分配评估
description: 使用视觉化饼图工具评估来访者在学习、社交、休息、娱乐等生活领域的时间投入占比，识别结构性失衡，激发对理想生活样态的具象化构想与渐进式调整动机。

name: CBT首次会谈：关系建立、结构化评估与目标协同设定
description: 在CBT取向的首次咨询中，通过共情锚定、结构化信息收集、问题归类与协作式目标生成，建立治疗联盟并确立1–3项具体、可测、分阶段的初步咨询目标。

name: cbu-dashboard
description: Скилл для автоматической загрузки банковской статистики с сайта Центрального банка Республики Узбекистан (cbu.uz) и построения интерактивного HTML-дашборда с анализом динамики показателей по всем коммерческим банкам. Используй этот скилл всякий раз, когда пользователь хочет: - скачать отчёты / статистику / данные с cbu.uz или ЦБУ или Центробанка Узбекистана - построить дашборд по банкам Узбекистана - проанализировать динамику показателей банков (активы, кредиты, капитал, депозиты) - найти банки с отрицательной динамикой или риском потери лицензии - обновить / пересобрать дашборд из уже скачан…

name: cbu-premium-static-report
description: Cloud Between Us에서 유료($2.99) 구매 유저에게 제공할 프리미엄 리포트를 LLM 없이 정적 메타데이터로 생성한다. 6×6(36) 조합을 규칙+템플릿+메타데이터로 커버하며, 세계관 톤(하늘/구름 서사)과 금지 규칙(진단/숫자/퍼센트)을 강제한다. 유료 리포트 카피/데이터/생성 로직/검증/유지보수 작업 시 사용.

name: cbvalidation
description: Use this skill when validating user input in ColdBox/BoxLang using cbvalidation. Covers constraint definitions, validate()/validateOrFail() calls, built-in validators, custom validators, shared constraint files, error handling in handlers, and integrating validation results with views and REST APIs.

name: cbwire
description: Use this skill when building reactive UI components in ColdBox/BoxLang with cbwire, a Livewire-inspired library. Covers wire components and templates, wire:model and wire:click directives, lifecycle hooks, computed properties, events, validation, file uploads, lazy loading, JavaScript integration, and the behavior traps that are hard to diagnose.

name: cbz-workflow
description: 检查、合并、拆分、修复和重命名本地 CBZ，并维护 ComicInfo.xml 与可逆合并元数据；用于实际 CBZ 文件处理。

name: cell-boundary-intersection-over-min-area-quantification
description: Use when segmentation was run on overlapping image patches and you need to quantify whether per-patch masks conflict at patch seams before merging them into final cell polygons.

name: cell-boundary-polygon-export
description: Use when a Sopa-processed SpatialData object (e.g. a tuto.zarr store) must be converted into Xenium Explorer input files — experiment.xenium, pyramidal .ome.tif image, cell boundary polygons, and cell category files — for visualization.

name: cell-by-bin-matrix-construction
description: Use when raw scATAC-seq fragment/BAM data must be converted into a snap-format cell-by-bin count matrix (e.g., at 5-kb resolution) as the starting feature representation for clustering or dimensionality reduction without population-level peak calling.

name: cell-by-cluster-enrichment-scoring
description: Use when an AnnData object has log-cpm normalised scRNA-seq data with tentative (ideally over-clustered) Leiden labels and you need per-cell enrichment scores against every cluster's marker signature to support significance-based cluster merging.

name: cell-by-feature-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have a per-cell sparse k-mer abundance matrix (from jellyfish counts) and a CKG look-up table (from simhash), and need a normalized cells-by-CKGs feature matrix for downstream cell type classification.

name: cell-by-peak-anndata-construction
description: Use when single-cell calling cards qbed insertions and called peaks (e.g., 902 Brd4 peaks from mouse cortex GSE148448) must be converted into a cell-by-peak count matrix for integration with Scanpy gene-expression AnnData.

name: cell-calling-method-benchmarking
description: Use when a raw unfiltered gene-by-barcode count matrix (mtx or h5) from droplet-based scRNA/snRNA-seq needs cell-calling, and multiple callers must be compared against ground-truth labels (HTO singlet/doublet or demuxlet genotypes).

name: cell-capacity-report
description: Produce a read-only, per-cell capacity report from AMP metrics — DB count, page-cache commit, and disk used against the A12 caps — and recommend add-cell vs rebalance plus flag tenants projected to outgrow a node. Use before scaling a geo, during weekly capacity review, or when a placement looks tight.

name: Cell-Cell Communication Analysis (CellChat)
description: ✅ **Use when:** - You have an annotated scRNA-seq dataset (Seurat object with cell type labels) - You want to identify ligand-receptor interactions between cell types - You want to visualize communication networks (chord diagrams, bubble plots) - You want to find dominant sender/receiver cell populations - **Chains from** `scrnaseq-seurat-core-analysis` output (`seurat_processed.rds`)

name: cell-cell-communication
description: Infer ligand-receptor signaling between cell types from scRNA-seq (and spatial) data. TRIGGER when the user mentions CellChat, CellPhoneDB, LIANA, NicheNet, Squidpy, "ligand-receptor", "cell-cell communication", "CCC", "intercellular signaling", "macrophage-T-cell crosstalk", "M1/M2 signaling", or has annotated single-cell data and wants to know which cell types are talking to which.

name: cell-cell-communication
description: Infer ligand-receptor signaling networks from annotated single-cell RNA-seq data and produce publication-ready communication plots. Use when you have a Seurat object with cell type labels and want to map sender/receiver/mediator roles, pathway activity, or cell-cell interaction matrices.

name: cell-cell-communication-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing ligand-receptor scoring rules for cell-cell communication inference on scRNA-seq data and you need an apples-to-apples benchmark on the same interaction database, same input matrix, and same permutation/significance pipeline.

name: cell-cell-communication-inference-from-scrnaseq
description: Use when scRNA-seq data has cluster/cell-type annotations and the goal is to compute transcriptome-based communication scores between sender and receiver clusters and rank specific ligand-receptor pairs (e.g., checkpoints, chemokines).

name: cell-cell-communication-matrix-factorization
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq expression (genes x cells) plus cell labels and need species-agnostic cell-cell communication inference, especially when no curated L-R database exists for the species or condition-specific shared vs unique signals are of interest.

name: cell-cell-communication-method-benchmarking
description: Use when single-cell RNA-Seq data must be interrogated for ligand-receptor interactions with multiple CCC methods, or when per-method interaction scores need to be combined into a robust consensus ranking via LIANA.

name: cell-cell-communication-module-interpretation
description: Use when you have pre-computed ligand-receptor CCI predictions (e.g., from CellChat on a scRNA-seq dataset such as GSE72056 melanoma) and need to biologically interpret which interaction groups/signals characterize a specific sender or receiver cell type.

name: cell-cell-communication-network-analysis
description: Use when you have clustered scRNA-seq cell groups and need to infer significant ligand-receptor communication between them, quantify pathway-level signaling, identify dominant senders/receivers, and group coordinated outgoing/incoming patterns.

name: cell-cell-communication-network-inference
description: Use when single-cell-resolution spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., seqFISH+ mouse cortex, Seq-Scope mouse colon) with a gene expression matrix plus cell spatial coordinates and cell-type labels is available, and the goal is to estimate which neighboring cell types regulate HVG expression.

name: cell-cell-communication-score-computation
description: Use when you need to quantify communication potential between an input cell population and partner cell types from transcriptomic data, e.g. comparing outward signaling of CAF-S1 vs CAF-S4 or LPS-stimulated DCs against the Primary Cell Atlas.

name: cell-cell-distance-based-communication-analysis
description: Use when you have non-spatial scRNA-seq data plus a limited spatial measurement of a few genes, and need to infer cell-cell communication or the spatial distance/range of a signaling pathway (e.g. Wg ~100 µm, Dpp ~125 µm).

name: cell-cell-distance-inference-from-transport-plan
description: Use when you have a fitted SpaOTsc transport plan γ* (n cells × m spatial positions) plus a spatial position distance matrix, and you need a pairwise spatial cell-cell distance matrix for downstream signaling or clustering analyses.

name: cell-cell-interaction-expression-profiling
description: Use when you have developmental series scRNA-seq (e.g., GSE153164 corticogenesis) with inferred L-R pair expression-change values and need to group interactions by temporal activity to pinpoint key developmental time points.

name: cell-cell-interaction-label-aggregation
description: Use when training or benchmarking a supervised CCI inference model (e.g., DeepCCI's ResNet+GCN interaction model) and per-method significant-interaction calls must be merged into a single consensus label set for classification.

name: cell-cell-interaction-network-comparison
description: Use when validating AI-inferred single-cell data against a real-profiled ground-truth cohort: you have matched (semi-profiled vs real-profiled) single-cell datasets with shared cell-type annotations and need a quantitative fidelity metric for cell-cell interaction inference.

name: cell-cell-interaction-network-degree-analysis
description: Use when bulk transcriptome + survival data have been reduced to prognostic immune marker gene pairs (IMGPs) and you need to rank cell types by favorable vs unfavorable prognostic associations via network degree.

name: cell-cell-interaction-network-inference
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix, cell-type labels, and time-point annotations and need to infer which ligand-receptor interactions connect which sender/receiver cell types at a given time point.

name: cell-cell-interaction-risk-score-modeling
description: Use when bulk transcriptomes with matched survival data (e.g., TCGA SKCM06 plus GSE validation cohorts) are available and a prognostic model must aggregate interaction-linked marker gene pairs into one risk score.

name: cell-cell-signaling-perturbation-scoring
description: Use when comparing cell–cell signaling between two tissue systems (e.g., IFN-stimulated vs. control PBMCs from SeuratData 'ifnb') and you need to rank edges where ligand and receptor are both significantly perturbed, whether concordantly or discordantly.

name: cell-citation
description: Use to convert references to Cell Press author–date style — in-text "(Smith et al., 2021)", an alphabetical reference list by first author with full author lists, journal names spelled out. This is the OPPOSITE of Science's numbered-by-appearance style.

name: cell-classification-cross-tabulation
description: Use when two cell-level AML/tumor classification labels exist for the same barcodes (e.g., CNA-based CONICSmat clusters vs. SNV/expression-based genotype calls) and you must quantify how well one predicts the other.

name: cell-cluster-marker-transposon-identification
description: Use when you have a processed scRNA-Seq BAM file and need to find which TEs (at locus resolution) are differentially expressed markers of specific cell clusters, e.g. cancer vs normal cell types.

name: cell-clustering-ari-evaluation
description: Use when you have simulated or labeled scRNA-seq data with known cell-type labels and need to quantify how well a normalization/confounding-removal method (e.g., scPLS) preserves cluster structure via ARI.

name: cell-clustering-validation-with-marker-genes
description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering result (e.g., from scSPARKL on a mixed-species sample like the Jurkat–293T mixture) must be checked against known marker genes and a ground-truth cell partition.

name: cell-code-review
description: Review a dewstack tutorial's runnable code — every sql cell=, py cell=, app= cell, and every site= HTML/CSS/JS block — for pedagogical code quality: semantic names over single letters, comments that explain why rather than restate what, read in the context of the surrounding prose. Use when asked to review, clean up, or improve code quality/naming/comments in one or more tutorials, or after writing new tutorial code that should be checked before it ships.

name: cell-collective-database-model-retrieval
description: Use when a refined GRN (adjacency matrix) must be converted into a draft Boolean Network and curated Boolean functions are available in the Cell Collective for the organism under study.

name: cell-communication
description: Workflow for ligand-receptor communication inference in single-cell or spatial data with sender-receiver summaries and cautious interpretation.

name: cell-communication
description: Cell-cell / ligand-receptor communication analysis for single-cell data using LIANA+ (recommended consensus default), CellPhoneDB, CellChat (R), and squidpy's ligrec. Use for inferring cell-cell communication, ligand-receptor pairs, source->target signaling from an annotated .h5ad. Trigger terms - "cell-cell communication", "ligand-receptor", "CellPhoneDB", "CellChat", "LIANA", "cell interaction", "ligrec".

name: cell-communication-cellphonedb
description: Analyze cell-cell communication using CellPhoneDB statistical method to identify significant ligand-receptor interactions between cell types via permutation testing.

name: cell-communication-gene-labeling
description: Use when an HVG list (e.g. from FindVariableFeatures(), variance, scannpy, or M3drop on seqFISH+/Seq-Scope data) must be split into communication-related (Y) vs non-related (N) genes via GeneCards/GO labels.

name: cell-communication-liana
description: Analyze cell-cell communication using LIANA+ to identify significant ligand-receptor interactions between cell types. (Recommended!)

name: cell-communication-network-extraction
description: Use when you have a CPM-normalized single-cell expression matrix plus a cell-annotation metafile and want to predict which ligand–receptor pairs mediate communication between annotated cell types.

name: cell-communication-statistics-summary
description: Use when a single-cell atlas (e.g. Tabula Muris, ~117 cell types) has been processed with NATMI and you need organism-wide summary metrics of autocrine signalling, such as the median number of co-detected ligand–receptor pairs per cell type.

name: cell-composition-differential-testing-along-pseudotime
description: Decision support for detecting condition- or covariate-associated changes in cell abundance/density along a multi-sample scRNA-seq pseudotime trajectory (Lamian TCD/XCD testing).

name: cell-connectivity-estimation-from-single-cell-data
description: Use when you have a set of minimum spanning trees (one per Totem/CLARA clustering, constructed with Slingshot) and need per-cell connectivity values in [0,1] to rank clusterings and identify likely trajectory leaves and branch points.

name: cell-connectivity-profiling
description: Use when the input is a single-cell expression dataset (SingleCellExperiment) expected to follow a linear, bifurcating, or multifurcating tree trajectory, and you need to rank candidate clusterings and locate trajectory leaves and branch points without a prior clustering.

name: cell-connectivity-summary-edge-aggregation
description: Use when NATMI ExtractEdges.py output edges exist and the goal is to summarise the entire communication network to show how strongly or specifically each cell type communicates to every other cell type, identifying highly communicating cell-type pairs or communities.

name: cell-connectivity-vector-analysis
description: Use when a Totem analysis has produced many candidate CLARA clusterings and you must automatically pick which one(s) to feed into Slingshot MST construction based on cell connectivity.

name: cell-count-scaling-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when you must show how reconstruction accuracy and sensitivity of a scGRN method depend on the number of input cells, and ground-truth regulatory edges (e.g., SERGIO-simulated 100-gene modules) are available for scoring.

name: cell-count-subsampling-scalability-analysis
description: Use when you must quantify the runtime, memory, and clustering-performance scaling of an integration/clustering method across increasing numbers of cells and compare it with alternatives.

name: cell-count-summary-reporting
description: Use when a VDJ preprocessing or filtering step (e.g. setupVdjPseudobulk) has just been applied and you must quantify and report how many cells were retained versus input, as a baseline check before downstream pseudobulking or trajectory analysis.

name: cell-coverage-outlier-filtering
description: Use when a raw single-cell ChIP-seq/scATAC-seq count matrix (cells x bins/peaks/TSS regions) contains low-quality or extreme-coverage cells that must be filtered before PCA, t-SNE/UMAP, or clustering.

name: cell-crowding-visualization
description: Use when evaluating whether a low-dimensional embedding of small UMI count matrices suffers from cell crowding at the latent origin, comparing vMF spherical vs Euclidean VAE latents or t-SNE/UMAP/PHATE baselines.

description: Use when evaluating how accurately an automatic cell-type annotation method labels clusters of scRNA-seq data against manually curated cell types, and a comparable consistent-rate table across multiple methods is needed.

name: cell-type-correlation-strategy-selection
description: Use when training a supervised single-cell label-assignment model on scRNA-seq data with known cell types and you must decide between a flat vs hierarchical classifier based on how highly correlated the training cell types are.

name: cell-type-correspondence-mapping
description: Use when visualizing two or more cellular-resolution SRT sections jointly (e.g., Stereo-seq axolotl DPI-10 vs DPI-15) and cell-type labels differ across sections, so naive default palettes misalign colors between biologically related or confusable cell types.

name: cell-type-count-aggregation
description: Use when you have a cell-by-feature scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq count matrix with per-cell type labels and need across-cell-type expression/accessibility profiles for Spearman/k-medoids clustering or Kendall's Tb correlation validation.

name: cell-type-count-matrix-aggregation
description: Use when a single-cell count matrix (e.g., scRNA-seq from MOSim sc_mosim) must be reduced to per-cell-type average profiles before clustering, PCA, or cross-omics correlation validation.

name: cell-type-deconvolution-method-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cell type identification or gene expression decomposition methods on simulated single-slice spatial transcriptomics benchmarks with paired scRNA-seq references and ground-truth per-cell assignments.

name: cell-type-deconvolution-wnnls
description: Use when estimating cell type proportions from bulk RNA-seq read counts with a multi-subject single-cell reference, especially for closely related cell types and without pre-selected marker genes.

name: cell-type-differential-abundance-testing
description: Use when a samples-by-features LC/MS intensity matrix (raw or batch-corrected) has group labels and the goal is to rank or count metabolomic features that differ between groups at a relaxed FDR threshold such as ≤ 0.2.

name: cell-type-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when a single-cell dataset contains annotated cell types and two conditions, and you need per-cell-type DE gene counts and magnitudes to rank the biological response across populations.

name: cell-type-disjoint-cross-validation-splitting
description: Use when benchmarking cross-modality translation methods (e.g., scRNA-seq to scATAC-seq) for generalization to cell types absent from training, mimicking the MB/MCC/MK/PBMC unseen-cell-type evaluation.

name: cell-type-drug-response-ranking
description: Use when you need to identify which cell type in an untreated disease scRNA-seq dataset is most responsive to a drug with a known target gene, without paired treated/untreated samples.

name: cell-type-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when SINCERA hierarchical clustering has produced cell clusters and each cluster must be annotated with a predicted cell type using differentially expressed genes and a Fisher's exact test against the EBI Expression Atlas annotation table.

name: cell-type-entropy-coefficient-of-variation-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing segmentation methods on spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., MERSCOPE melanoma, CosMx lung) where no pixel-level ground truth exists and you need reference-based homogeneity vs cell-size consistency metrics.

name: cell-type-epiallele-trajectory-comparison
description: Use when comparing methylated-core/epiallele structures across purified cell populations (e.g., astrocytes, neurons, MOEs from cerebellum and cortex) to test for shared precursor cores during postnatal differentiation.

name: cell-type-expression-aggregation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq study stored as an AnnData/H5AD object must be loaded into a relational sparse expression table and queried for gene-level per-cell-type averages, e.g. to replicate Cellenium's server-side aggregation.

name: cell-type-expression-specificity-ranking
description: Use when a query gene of interest (e.g. 'insulin') must be matched to the annotated cell types that specifically express it, within one study or across multiple ingested scRNA-seq studies.

name: cell-type-f1-score-computation
description: Use when comparing label-transfer accuracy of scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq integration methods on cells with held-out ground-truth annotations, especially under varying annotation budgets.

name: cell-type-flux-differential-testing
description: Use when per-cell metabolic fluxes have been predicted from scRNA-seq (scFEA) and must be compared across reported cell-type labels (e.g. cancer, myeloid, T cells) to test which population has the highest glucose metabolic rate.

name: cell-type-fraction-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples have been deconvolved against a single-cell reference (e.g., via scPlant decomposeBulk on an annotated Seurat object) and you need a heatmap of per-sample cell-type fractions to compare compositions across conditions.

name: cell-type-functional-annotation
description: Use when an unsupervised clustering (e.g., Leiden) of scRNA-seq data has produced clusters with no labels and you must assign a cell type from the functional enrichment of cluster-specific genes.

name: cell-type-gene-signature-definition
description: Use when cell types have been annotated across merged datasets (e.g., after Harmony-kernel integration and label propagation) and a unified marker-gene signature per type/subtype is needed, such as neuronal (LINGO2, CUX2, SST) and glial (SLC1A2, MBP, CLDN5) markers.

name: cell-type-ground-truth-precision-evaluation
description: Use when a real scRNA-seq dataset has trusted cell-type labels serving as ground truth and you need to quantify how precisely a gene-set or pathway score (TRS, scDRS) retrieves the trait-relevant cell type.

name: cell-type-held-out-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq integration methods on two datasets with known cell-type compositions and you want to verify that a cell type present in only one dataset is left unmatched instead of incorrectly aligned.

name: cell-type-hierarchy-construction
description: Use when training a custom Census cell-type annotation model from a scRNA-seq reference (e.g. Tabula Sapiens plus CCLE) that requires inferring the cell-type hierarchy and fitting node classifiers.

name: cell-type-homology-annotation
description: Use when integrating single-cell datasets from multiple species whose cell type annotations use different or dataset-specific ontology terms, and a shared cell type homology mapping is required before integration and scoring.

name: cell-type-hop-distance-computation
description: Use when you have an annotated SpatialData object (cell boundaries, cell-type labels, niche assignments) and need to test whether specific cell populations exclusively interact with themselves or are spatially restricted to particular niches.

name: cell-type-identification-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether joint (all-slices) inference improves cell type labeling accuracy of spatial transcriptomics methods, or when comparing ST cell type identification methods on simulated Visium data with known ground-truth single-cell labels.

name: cell-type-identification-performance-metrics
description: Use when comparing or tuning a scRNA-seq cell type identifier on annotated datasets and you need to quantify correct/erroneous assignments for known and unknown cell populations (C, E, EA, CUA, EUA).

name: cell-type-identification-potts-model-map-inference
description: Use when you need per-cell (not per-spot) discrete cell type labels for ST spots (Visium, Slide-seq), given nucleus segmentation outputs and a labeled scRNA-seq reference, with spatial smoothness enforced.

name: cell-type-importance-visualization
description: Use when you have dsCellNet-inferred ligand-receptor networks across multiple developmental time points (e.g., GSE153164 corticogenesis stages) and need per-cell-type incoming/outgoing/total edge counts to rank the most communicating cell types per stage.

name: cell-type-interaction-overlap-statistics
description: Use when gABC/ABC-scored enhancer-gene interactions have been predicted per cell type from snATAC-seq candidate enhancers and you need per-cell-type interaction counts plus cross-cell-type overlap/shared fractions.

name: cell-type-isoform-usage-aggregation
description: Use when SingleCellExperiment 3'UTR isoform count matrices (*.txs.Rds, *.genes.Rds) from scUTRquant must be summarized per cell type and genes labeled multi-UTR vs IPA under a ≥10% isoform-fraction cutoff.

name: cell-type-isoform-usage-analysis
description: Use when single-cell PacBio Iso-Seq data must be compared across cell types to identify which isoforms (e.g., ENST transcripts) dominate per cell type, or to test whether a gene undergoes major isoform switching.

name: cell-type-label-alignment-evaluation
description: Use when you have per-cell embeddings (e.g., tGPT transformer features) plus ground-truth cell type annotations and must quantify clustering alignment via NMI, ARI, and FMI.

name: cell-type-label-guided-bayesian-matrix-factorization
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices come with trusted cell type labels and the goal is dropout imputation that leverages those labels, e.g. benchmarking silhouette/Pearson clustering metrics against scImpute, DrImpute, PBLR.

name: cell-type-label-hierarchy-classification
description: Use when benchmarking marker gene panels against a two-layer cell-type label hierarchy on scRNA-seq data, or when testing whether fewer hierarchy-aware markers match a one-vs-all baseline panel.

name: cell-type-label-permutation-ablation
description: Use when benchmarking NeuronChat's projection prediction on retrograde-labeling ground truth and you must rule out that benchmark performance is driven by node cell-type labels rather than the specific ground-truth graph topology.

name: cell-type-label-permutation-testing
description: Use when constructing a cell–cell communication network from scRNA-seq data and you need to decide which sender–receiver L–R interactions are statistically significant rather than keeping all expression-product edges.

name: cell-type-label-prediction
description: Use when annotating cell types in scRNA-seq data without training on the test dataset, or when benchmarking a zero-shot label predictor against supervised classifiers like CellTypist on a multi-batch atlas such as the open-problems pancreas dataset.

name: cell-type-label-propagation-across-datasets
description: Use when multiple independent scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., three cortex studies totaling ~105,099 cells) are jointly integrated and one or more reference annotations must be propagated to unlabeled cells without re-clustering from scratch.

name: cell-type-label-supervised-feature-ranking
description: Use when building a Cellcano reference for scATAC-seq celltyping: the reference gene score matrix (from ArchR) has annotated cell type labels and features must be reduced to cell-type-specific genes before MLP training.

name: cell-type-marker-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a cell-type-specific gene network (weighted edge matrix) for one of 26 cell types and need to verify that its node scores recover the correct pangaloDB cell-type markers.

name: cell-type-marker-enrichment-annotation
description: Use when scQA clustering (labels.txt) has assigned cells to clusters and you must confirm each cluster's key genes overlap known markers, hub genes, and DEGs (e.g., endothelial ADTRP, CDH5, CLEC14A, ACVRL1).

name: cell-type-marker-enrichment-interpretation
description: Use when you have a gene marker list selected from scRNA-seq phenotypes and need to verify it recovers the correct tissues and cell types by enrichment against a curated reference set such as HuBMAP_ASCTplusB_augmented_2022.

name: cell-type-marker-gene-matrix-handling
description: Use when reconstructing or fine-tuning the DCNet network and you need to wire 9078 marker genes to 434 cell-type hidden neurons via the zero-one relation matrix and align input/output neuron ordering with index.pkl.

name: cell-type-marker-gene-selection
description: Use when you have a raw/normalized scRNA-seq count matrix paired with manually annotated cell-type labels and need a per-cell-type positive marker gene list to drive marker-based or marker-learning cell-type prediction.

name: cell-type-marker-gene-validation
description: Use when scBridge (or a baseline such as scJoint, Seurat or GLUE) has produced predicted cell-type labels on target scATAC/ADT data and you need marker-based evidence that the predicted populations (e.g. Naive vs Effector CD4+ T cells) are biologically correct.

name: cell-type-marker-gmv-inference
description: Use when you have an annotated single-cell dataset (e.g., the Field et al. week-2 cortical organoid data, GEO GSE106245) plus a cell type marker GMT file and want interpretable, module-level per-cell cell type activity rather than opaque clustering.

name: cell-type-marker-validation
description: Use when a single-cell TE matrix (scTE .h5ad output from scRNA-seq or scTEATAC output from scATAC-seq) has been clustered and you must confirm cell-type assignments or marker-TE specificity.

name: cell-type-marker-verification-from-loadings
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. SingleCellExperiment) has been embedded with correspondence analysis and you want to check whether high-loading genes correspond to known cell-type markers (e.g. GNLY, TYROBP, LYZ, S100A8, CD74, HLA-DRA) and interpret cell-population associations.

name: cell-type-matching-metric-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cross-species cell type matching pipelines (e.g., human vs mouse vs marmoset primary motor cortex scRNA-seq) and you need reproducible ADS/recall metrics, including gene-matching ablations that test whether ProtBERT gene matches outperform BLAST matches.

name: cell-type-mean-expression-profile-computation
description: Use when preparing labelled scRNA-seq training data (e.g. SingleCellExperiment objects with known cell labels) and you need per-cell-type mean expression profiles plus a cross-cell-type correlation matrix to decide a classifier strategy.

name: cell-type-neighborhood-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when single-cell data have been pseudo-spatially mapped onto ST spots (e.g., via STEM's netsc2st mapping) and the goal is to quantify spatial proximity/colocalization between rare cell types such as TSKs, endothelial cells, or pDCs.

name: cell-type-neighbourhood-proportion-computation
description: Use when comparing the fidelity of cell-to-cell neighbourhood (cell-cell association) structure between two spatial transcriptomics representations — e.g. bin2cell-reconstructed cells vs default 8 μm Visium HD bins — against an expert-annotated MERFISH reference.

name: cell-type-nomenclature-standardization
description: Use when combining marker gene sets from multiple published databases or cell-sorting sources whose gene symbols and cell type labels follow non-standard, inconsistent nomenclature, and you need harmonized, comparable sets.

name: cell-type-perturbation-detection
description: Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq count matrix with per-cell metadata assigning condition, patient, and cluster, and need to identify which predefined cell types are transcriptomically perturbed between two conditions.

name: cell-type-perturbation-ranking
description: Use when you have untreated diseased scRNA-seq data with cell-type annotations and a known drug target gene, and need to identify which cell types are drug-responsive or resistant without paired treated/untreated samples.

name: cell-type-phenotype-association-testing
description: Use when cell-type proportions have been estimated from bulk RNA-seq (via BisqueRNA bulk.props or BisqueMarker) and you need to test associations with phenotypes such as BMI, Matsuda index, or Braak stage, replicating reported cell-composition associations.

name: cell-type-positive-fraction-quantification
description: Use when single-cell AnnData atlases spanning multiple ages (e.g., Tabula Muris Senis, 328K cells, 19 tissues, 1-30 months) must be scored for senescence and aggregated into per-cell-type positive-cell proportions or old/young ratios.

name: cell-type-potency-ranking-analysis
description: Use when a scRNA-Seq count matrix with malignant/non-malignant or cell-type annotations is available and the goal is to estimate and rank differentiation potency of cell types without marker genes, feature selection, or training.

name: cell-type-prediction-confusion-matrix-computation
description: Use when you have Cellcano (or similar supervised) predicted cell-type labels for a target scATAC-seq dataset plus ground-truth labels (e.g., FACS-sorted FACS labels embedded in cell identifiers) and need to quantify per-class prediction accuracy.

name: cell-type-probability-classification
description: Use when single-cell expression data has a small labeled training set and you need probabilistic cell type predictions plus predictive entropy to guide cell selection or evaluate annotation uncertainty.

name: cell-type-probability-expression-correlation
description: Use when you need marker genes for cell types absent from training data, given OnClass prediction matrices (pred_Y_all.released.npy) and single-cell expression data such as Tabula Muris Senis FACS cells.

name: cell-type-profile-matching
description: Use when ST pixels are cell mixtures and you need to assign reference-free deconvolved cell-type transcriptional profiles to known cell populations and compare them across conditions (e.g., aged vs young) for perturbation-driven gene changes.

name: cell-type-proportion-accuracy-evaluation
description: Decision support for validating false-positive control of Scanpro proportion analysis on null simulations, and for choosing pseudo-replicate counts (2–14) based on total cell counts per condition (~1,000 to ~50,000 cells).

name: cell-type-proportion-computation-per-condition
description: Use when comparing cell-type composition of an AI-generated (semi-profiled) cohort against real-profiled single-cell ground truth across defined conditions, e.g. COVID-19 severity states (Healthy, Asymptomatic, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Critical).

name: cell-type-proportion-controlled-synthetic-data-generation
description: Use when you need a simulated scRNA-seq count matrix with known ground-truth cell-type labels and controlled per-type cell numbers — e.g. to benchmark clustering methods on a rare cell type (<5% of cells).

name: cell-type-proportion-correlation-analysis
description: Use when evaluating SC-ST mapping outputs (SC-ST / ST-SC mapping matrices) against ground-truth ST cell-type labels, to quantify whether each method preserves cell-type composition of spots rather than just coordinate accuracy.

name: cell-type-proportion-correlation-evaluation
description: Use when a decomposition method's estimated cell-type proportions (e.g., BisqueRNA's res$bulk.props) must be scored against known or reference proportions per individual and cell type using Pearson correlation and RMSD.

name: cell-type-proportion-quantification
description: Use when you have raw scRNA-seq UMI counts from a heterogeneous cell suspension (e.g. 68k PBMCs) and need cluster-level cell-type composition percentages validated against a published population breakdown.

name: cell-type-proportion-statistical-testing
description: Use when single-cell resolution data (AnnData with sample, cluster, condition metadata columns) needs differential compositional analysis of cell-type proportions, with or without biological replicates.

name: cell-type-proportion-summarization
description: Use when per-cell DA scores (or similar per-cell condition-association statistics) have been computed on an integrated single-cell dataset with cell-type annotations and you need to rank cell types by the fraction of cells linked to a condition such as severe disease.

name: cell-type-protein-profiling-integration
description: Use when you have co-registered IMC (protein imaging mass cytometry) and SIMS (secondary ion mass spectrometry for metabolites) data from the same tissue regions, cell segmentation masks, and need to assign cell types based on protein expression patterns, then overlay those assignments onto.

name: cell-type-purity-evaluation
description: Use when a joint latent embedding (e.g. scConfluence latent in mdata.obsm['latent']) must be quantitatively validated against known cell-type labels, as in diagonal-integration benchmarks or hyperparameter sensitivity sweeps.

name: cell-type-rank-dimension-reduction-visualization
description: Use when a scRank analysis has produced a ranked list of drug-responsive cell types (obj@cell_type_rank) and you need to check or display how the ranking distributes across single cells on a dimension-reduction embedding.

name: cell-type-recovery-assessment
description: Use when you have simulated scRNA-seq count data with known cell-type labels (e.g., from sc_mosim/SPARSim via MOSim) and need to quantify how well a clustering tool recovers the simulated cell populations.

name: cell-type-recovery-assessment-across-graining-levels
description: Use when selecting a graining level for metacell construction and you need to check that rare cell populations are not merged into other types, especially in datasets of varying complexity or size.

name: cell-type-recovery-auc-evaluation
description: Use when comparing pathway activity scoring methods on scRNA-seq data where ground-truth cell labels exist (e.g., SERGIO simulations or annotated datasets), to measure cell-type recovery AUC and accuracy.

name: cell-type-rejection-thresholding
description: Use when annotating single-cell RNA-seq cells via marker counting and you must conservatively reject low-confidence assignments (possible unknown cell types) before downstream cluster reassignment.

name: cell-type-relationship-tree-inference
description: Use when you need to assess whether a subsampled ('sketched') single-cell dataset preserves cross-study cell-type subtype relationships, by harmonizing labels with CellHint and comparing the inferred relationship tree against a full-data reference tree.

name: cell-type-relative-interaction-quantification
description: Use when several pre-computed cell-cell communication (CCI) datasets from different conditions must be compared cell-type-wise, to test whether a cell type (e.g., mast cells or NKT-p) consistently mediates more interactions in one condition.

name: cell-type-replicability-subsampling-simulation
description: Use when you must stress-test whether a cross-dataset cell-type identification method still recovers a target type that is rare (1–20% of cells) and only subtly different from the out-group, rather than well-separated abundant types.

name: cell-type-scaling-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether a transcriptomic perturbation score (e.g., number of DEGs, scDist distance) scales with the number of cells per cell type in single-cell RNA-seq data, or when benchmarking speed of differential-state methods.

name: cell-type-scatter-plot-visualization
description: Use when a small marker-gene panel has been selected and you need a visual check that the reduced-dimensional projection separates known cell type labels into distinct clusters, e.g., reproducing a published t-SNE of cells projected onto 15 markers.

name: cell-type-score-aggregation-across-clusters
description: Use when you have a cell-type-by-cell score matrix (es.max) from sctype_score() and Seurat cluster identities and must assign a single label per cluster, with an Unknown fallback for low-confidence assignments.

name: cell-type-score-computation
description: Use when you have EpiRegio GeneQuery REM tables (regressionCoefficient, per-cell-type DNase1 signal) for a gene and need cell type-specific REM contributions to gene expression.

name: cell-type-score-computation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq analysis requires scoring cells against known cell-type markers (e.g., producing per-cell scores/labels for MASI-based annotation or for pipeline variants in integration benchmarks).

name: cell-type-score-ranking-of-rems
description: Use when a set of REMs from an EpiRegio Gene Query must be prioritized by cell type/tissue specificity (e.g. 'heart') before downstream TF motif enrichment such as PASTAA.

name: cell-type-score-space-centroid-distance-analysis
description: Use when transferring labels from a reference atlas with MASI and query data may contain cell types not present in the reference: cells whose closest-centroid distance approaches their farthest-centroid distance (ratio near 1, certainty near 0) should be flagged as unassigned.

name: cell-type-separation-visualization
description: Use when a VEGA (or similar interpretable VAE) model has been trained on single-cell RNA-seq with gene-module-wired latents and you must check that latent dimensions separate annotated cell populations before interpreting module activities.

name: cell-type-signature-deconvolution
description: Use when you need to infer relative cell type composition from bulk RNA-seq by scoring curated cell-type gene signatures (GMT module lists) with sample-level PC1 module activity rather than a regression-based deconvolution tool.

name: cell-type-silhouette-and-batch-entropy-metrics
description: Use when comparing cell-type annotation or integration methods on the same labeled multi-batch scRNA-seq datasets and you need standardized scores (silhouette, batch entropy, F1, accuracy) plus statistical significance.

name: cell-type-similarity-quartile-stratification
description: Use when evaluating BIRD-predicted differential DH between many cell-type pairs and you need to know how prediction–truth correlation (Pearson, all loci vs differential loci) depends on the similarity of the two cell types' DH profiles.

name: cell-type-spatial-distance-quantification
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells have been projected into a spatially informed pseudo-space and you need to test whether the spatial proximity between annotated cell types differs between biological conditions (e.g., normal vs. disease).

name: cell-type-specific-co-expression-inference
description: Use when raw UMI-count scRNA-seq data need cell-type-specific co-expression networks, when correlation-based methods give inflated false positives due to sequencing depth confounding, or when differential co-expression between disease groups is sought.

name: cell-type-specific-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g. BALF or PBMC count matrices from GEO) has been clustered and cell-type-annotated, and the goal is to test candidate genes (e.g. MCEMP1, HLA-DRA, ETS1) for differential expression between severity groups per cell type.

name: cell-type-specific-differential-peak-analysis
description: Use when single-cell CC/qbed insertion data (e.g., Brd4 mouse cortex, GSE148448) must be converted to a cell-by-peak AnnData and differential TF binding peaks per cell type must be linked to nearby gene expression.

name: cell-type-specific-enhancer-motif-ranking
description: Use when you have trained BOM/XGBoost classifiers on cell-type-specific distal regulatory elements (e.g. mouse E8.25 scATAC-derived CREs) and need per-motif SHAP importance rankings plus local explanations at a locus of interest.

name: cell-type-specific-gene-expression-identification
description: Use when single-cell expression data for known cell types (e.g., Astro, MG, L2/3, Vip) and per-cell nested TLD boundary calls are available and you need to designate genes or boundaries as cell-type-specific.

name: cell-type-specific-gene-thresholding
description: Use when running deCS.fisher on a marker gene list or GWAS trait-associated gene list and you must first convert a cell type specificity score panel into discrete per-cell-type gene sets via a score cutoff.

name: cell-type-specific-genomic-data-integration
description: Use when scoring structural variants (inversions, translocations, deletions, duplications) with hg19 breakpoints against phenotypes like head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system or pituitary to identify causative genes and coding vs long-range.

name: cell-type-specific-ipa-usage-comparison
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq alignments and InPACT-derived IPA usage estimates are available and the goal is to flag IPA events whose usage is restricted to one cell type versus others.

name: cell-type-specific-locus-annotation
description: Use when DA peaks or age-related expression changes from PBMC ATAC-seq/RNA-seq must be assigned to cell-type-specific loci to test whether aging signatures (e.g., B cell decline) are shared or sex-specific between men and women.

name: cell-type-specific-loop-summit-annotation
description: Use when scHi-C-derived loops from matched cell type subsets (e.g. 261-cell astrocyte/microglia/ODC/L2/3 neuron SnapHiC runs) need epigenomic and expression validation against matched bulk references.

name: cell-type-specific-model-validation
description: Use when a model trained on paired bulk omics data (e.g., TCGA miRNA-mRNA) must be validated for cell-type-specific inference against scRNA-seq data with known cell-type miRNA profiles (e.g., Isakova Kidney-Breast-Skin GSE151334).

name: cell-type-specific-network-annotation
description: Use when you have cell-type-specific gene/GRN networks (edge-score matrices per cell type) and need to validate biological relevance via TF, cell-type-marker, and ENCODE TF-target enrichment before benchmarking inference methods.

name: cell-type-specific-pseudobulk-mixed-model-fitting
description: Use when per-individual, per-cell-type scRNA-seq data must be aggregated into CTP/ctnu/P pseudobulk inputs and fit with CTMM linear mixed models to quantify or test cell type-specific interindividual variance (and its differentiation between cell types/stages).

name: cell-type-specific-regression-metrics-evaluation
description: Use when predicted and true count matrices must be scored per cell type for multiple prediction scenarios (within-batch/cross-batch, in-sample/out-of-sample) and compared against baselines like scGen and scPreGAN.

name: cell-type-specific-regulatory-landscape-integration
description: Use when interpreting patient structural variants (inversions, deletions, duplications, translocations) whose pathogenic effect is suspected to be non-coding/long-range, and cell type-specific enhancer and TAD data are needed to nominate disease genes.

name: cell-type-specific-regulatory-variant-mapping
description: Use when mapping enhancer-resident noncoding GWAS SNPs to putative target genes via cell type-specific chromatin loops (SnapHiC *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe), e.g. neuropsychiatric SNPs in human prefrontal cortex.

name: cell-type-specific-rem-filtering
description: Use when submitting a gene list to EpiRegio's Gene Query and you need REMs restricted to a relevant cell type or tissue context rather than genome-wide REMs.

name: cell-type-specific-spatial-de-testing
description: Use when the goal is to identify genes whose spatial expression varies within a specific cell type — e.g. testing whether imputation of non-MERFISH genes into a MERFISH slice increases detectable cell-type-specific spatially DE genes.

name: cell-type-specific-variance-component-estimation
description: Use when scRNA-seq counts with cell and individual metadata need to be summarized into cell type-specific pseudobulk and tested for genes with significant cell type-specific interindividual expression variance.

name: cell-type-specificity-reference-panel-matching
description: Use when a preprocessed, z-scored cluster-level marker-gene expression matrix (clusters as columns) needs automatic cell type labels matched against a human cell type reference panel such as MonacoImmune or BlueprintEncode.

name: cell-type-specificity-score-implementation
description: Use when annotating clusters of a processed scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Seurat object with scaled matrix) against a tissue-restricted marker database using both positive and negative markers, or when verifying a from-scratch reimplementation of the ScType scoring algorithm.

name: cell-type-specificity-tscore-estimation
description: Use when building or verifying deCS CTGene reference panels: you need per-cell-type ranked gene lists derived from bulk (t-score) or single-cell (z-score) specificity scores before annotation or enrichment.

name: cell-type-stratified-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when you have an integration-adjusted expression matrix plus raw logcounts, consensus cell-type labels and per-sample severity metadata, and need to quantify whether integration improves cell-type-stratified prediction accuracy.

name: cell-type-stratified-integration-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq integration methods on datasets with imbalanced cell type proportions, where a cell type-aware batch-mixing metric (rather than plain iLISI) is needed to score batch mixing per cell type.

name: cell-type-stratified-prediction-assessment
description: Use when predicting held-out condition/batch scRNA-seq matrices (e.g., PW034-705) and you must judge prediction accuracy separately per cell type under both condition-only and condition-plus-batch scenarios.

name: che-interrogate
description: Pre-planning readiness gate — the skeptical interrogator. Runs on the RAW input (ticket(s), PRD, brief, existing SPEC) inside che-spec §1.6, and on the approved/draft SPEC inside che-act §0.6 before scope capture. Checks sufficiency, internal coherence (including contradictions across multiple tickets), consistency with the code already implemented, past decisions, established conventions and — last — market practice. Emits a bounded set of high-leverage questions and blocks on BLOCKER/MAJOR only. Max 5 questions per round, max 2 rounds. Invoke ONLY from che-spec and che-act, never standalone.

name: che-knowledge
description: Create and evolve the project's durable knowledge base: glossary.md (vocabulary) plus <domain>/conventions.md (observed practice per domain). Evidence-based, previewed as a dry-run diff and gated by keep/alter/revert before every write. Invoked at phase boundaries by che-architect, che-archeology, che-spec and che-act, or standalone via /che-knowledge.

name: che-manual-plan
description: Generates or updates the manual test plan as an EXECUTABLE contract: creates the plan when none exists, migrates a legacy prose plan when one does, and fills each acceptance criterion's ```yaml block (driver, lane, steps, locators, assertions, evidence) from the session context. Deterministic scaffolding and the gate live in `che manual-plan sync` + `che manual-plan validate`; this skill authors the content. Idempotent — re-running never destroys prose or an existing contract. Consumed by che-manual-test-executor (runs it) and che-manual-verification (renders it for a non-technical tester).

name: che-manual-test-executor
description: Executes a manual test plan's EXECUTABLE CONTRACTS step by step using the Chrome DevTools MCP for UI and the terminal for HTTP/API calls, producing evidence per step (screenshots, optional video, console and network logs, API responses) and a structured pass/fail report per acceptance criterion. Requires a plan that passes `che manual-plan validate`; migrates nothing itself. Call it AFTER che-manual-plan and BEFORE che-ship, or standalone with a worktree + plan path.

name: che-manual-test-executor
description: Executes the manual_test_plan.md step-by-step using Playwright MCP (browser interactions + screenshots) or HTTP/curl requests for API-only scenarios, generates evidence files (PNG screenshots, JSON logs), and delivers a structured pass/fail report per AC. Call this AFTER manual_test_plan.md is written by che-act and BEFORE che-ship, or standalone when user passes a worktree + task-id or a manual test plan path explicitly.

name: che-manual-verification

name: che-mcp-audit

Use when asked to "audit my MCP setup", "clean up MCP servers", "which MCP should I keep", "too many MCP servers", "convert MCP to CLI", or to harden MCP config on a new machine/VPS. Proven 2026-06-27 (Mac: 37→12 servers).

name: che-merge-resolver

NEVER decides ambiguous cases alone. Every resolution logged with decisions.log MERGE_RESOLVE entries.

Registry stays OUTSIDE user worktree in $CHE_SESSIONS_ROOT/.registry/projects/<slug>/. DOES NOT create anything in the worktree unless the user explicitly asks VERBATIM.

name: che-pair

Blocks only CRITICAL/HIGH and only with a cited rule; bounded to max 2 rounds per slice with a no-progress stop and an A/B/C escalation menu. Shifts quality left WITHOUT replacing che-ship. Invoke ONLY from che-act §2, never standalone.

name: che-pdf-mcp

Invoke when user passes a PR URL and asks to process review comments, or when /che-pr-comments is called.

name: che-qa

name: che-refactor
description: Behaviour-preserving refactoring in the Fowler sense. Takes existing code and applies established refactorings (extract function, inline, extract variable, replace conditional with polymorphism, split phase, ...) to improve readability, maintainability, scalability and testability WITHOUT changing observable behaviour. PRECONDITION: a green test safety net; if coverage is missing the first step is characterization tests, not refactoring. Each step is small, tests green after it, atomic commit. Invocable standalone and recommendable by che-pair. NEVER run inside che-ship.

name: che-seo-demand-analytics

name: che-seo-geo-auditor-pro

name: che-session-recover
description: Triage and recover Claude Code sessions after a crash (VS Code quit, OOM, accidental close). Use when the user says "recover sessions", "what was I working on", "VS Code crashed", "lost my sessions", "which sessions had unfinished work", or after any unexpected editor/terminal shutdown.

name: che-ship
description: End-of-task ship command. After: atomic conventional commits on worktree, git push, opens DRAFT PR against default branch with structured description, assigns PR to user. Invoke ONLY after all che tasks DONE, or when user explicitly runs /che-ship.

name: che-simplify
description: Produces a SIMPLIFICATION PLAN for something already planned or implemented (epic, task graph, gh-stack plan, module, codebase area). Applies the Simplicity Bias (engineering-contracts §1) with the GOALS held fixed: it classifies every element as essential or accidental complexity, then proposes the smallest plan that still meets the goals — merging slices, deferring items, collapsing PR layers, removing unearned abstractions. Output is a spec-shaped plan plus a decision trail. NEVER a verdict (that is che-code-review) and NEVER a pure explanation (that is che-explain).

name: check-the-descriptor

name: check-the-device

Makes the agent confirm real, current API signatures before using them, instead of inventing plausible-but-wrong calls from memory.

name: check-the-edges

name: check-the-evidence

name: check-the-findings

name: check-the-stage-records
