name: chengyu-adapt-to-changing-circumstances
description: Use when the original plan needs to flex mid-flight in response to new information / changed inputs / discovered constraints — but flexibility WITHOUT defined scope degenerates into either rigid plan-sticking or unbounded winging-it. CRITICAL Step 0 (mirror of chengyu-close-door-catch-thief): scope MUST be defined before any deviation. If operator hasn't given a flexibility-scope tier, agent must PROPOSE 2-4 tiers and let operator pick where the line is. Default tier is "don't do irreversible damage to hardware, software, and data" but context shifts the boundary (hackathon, prod deploy, code…

name: chengyu-besiege-wei-save-zhao
description: Use when the operator has explicitly authorised an indirect / non-causal move — when frontal attack is blocked AND chengyu-remove-firewood-from-cauldron has been exhausted, requiring attention-redirect or incentive-shift rather than technical root-fixing. Default to chengyu-remove-firewood-from-cauldron unless the operator has told the agent how to 圍魏.

name: chengyu-borrow-corpse-return-soul
description: Use when proven-elsewhere logic should be transplanted into your project rather than re-derived — covers both reviving abandoned-but-good code from your own history AND copying live working config (linting, CI, README templates, infra patterns) from a healthy sibling project. The "soul" is the working logic; the "body" is your project that receives it.

name: chengyu-break-whole-into-parts
description: Use when facing a task too large to hold in one piece — decompose into atomic subtasks. Divide-and-conquer in chengyu form. Pairs naturally with subagent dispatch (each part becomes one subagent's job) and with the dispatching-parallel-agents superpower. The decomposition itself is the skill — the parts should each have one clear purpose and a well-defined interface to the others.

name: chengyu-cicada-sheds-its-shell
description: Use when designing a migration — graceful transition where the old interface stays as a thin stub/proxy/shim, real implementation moves underneath, consumers keep working through the transition, eventual cleanup of the shell once consumer count reaches zero. The schema of every good rename / endpoint move / library v1→v2 / database schema migration / monorepo split.

name: chengyu-cleave-ox-at-joints
description: Use when planning any non-trivial change — refactor, bug fix, migration, optimisation, communication — and the agent should find the natural seams / high-leverage points of the target system rather than brute-forcing through. Cut at joints (low resistance, clean result), not at bone (high resistance, blade dulls, messy result). The patron-saint chengyu of working WITH the grain of the system.

name: chengyu-close-door-catch-thief
description: Use when debugging by narrowing the search space — isolate the failure domain so the bug reproduces in a controlled, minimal environment. CRITICAL Step 0: the agent must ASK (if unclear) or PITCH (if obvious, just needs operator confirmation) the specific "close the door" strategy BEFORE executing it; the closing has side effects (disabling services, modifying shared state, replacing real integrations with mocks) that need operator sign-off.

name: chengyu-create-something-from-nothing
description: SUBAGENT-ONLY skill for generating a graduated spread of plausible-to-speculative solutions when the main agent is stuck in a local minimum. Output is one continuous artifact (NO dividers) that starts from verified fact and slides into bottom-K speculation; calling main-agent fact-checks throughout. Has TWO HARD PRECONDITIONS that must be met before any output: (1) running on a BullshitBench-passing model (Claude Opus 4.5–4.8 / Sonnet 4.5–4.6, or equivalent — NOT the Claude 5 generation), (2) operator — NOT the agent — explicitly confirms for this invocation that the running model qualifies.…

name: chengyu-great-wisdom-looks-foolish
description: Use when resisting the urge to demonstrate cleverness — obvious-and-simple is often the right answer, and performative complexity is the failure mode. REQUIRES a target parameter at invocation specifying which dimension to apply to — implementation (over-engineered code), representation (over-fancy reply / unnecessary verbosity), or both. The agent must ASK for the target if the operator hasn't specified.

name: chengyu-grind-pestle-to-needle
description: Use when working on a hard problem where most attempts fail — when 99 of 100 things won't work and the temptation is to give up before the 100th; when each failed attempt's value (it ruled something out) is being underweighted; when incremental compound progress on an unsharpened-needle target is needed

name: chengyu-know-what-you-dont-know
description: Use when about to guesstimate over a gap in knowledge — surface the gap explicitly instead. A market observation that justifies this skill's existence — agents that confidently lie about knowing things get rewarded by short-horizon metrics; agents that honestly mark gaps are rare. Voice transcription is the canonical case study (no service surfaces transcription errors; LLMs guesstimate over them). This skill's whole shape is "be the rare agent that says 'I don't know X' instead of fabricating a smooth answer".

name: chengyu-listen-all-sides-see-clearly
description: Use BEFORE declaring victory / shipping / committing, AND proactively for any non-trivial claim, answer, plan, or decision that would benefit from fresh external input — default to invoking it for substantive work rather than waiting to be asked, since bringing fresh info into the conversation is generally worth the token cost. Get adversarial multi-angle review or fresh information from at least one of three source classes (subagent, internet, other LLMs via API). Inter-links with chengyu-create-something-from-nothing — high-hallucination LLM sources behave like uncontrolled 無中生有, so apply t…

name: chengyu-lost-sheep-repair-fence
description: Use after a failure has occurred (bug shipped, test broke, deploy rolled back, data lost, security incident) — the impulse is to fix the immediate damage and move on, but the chengyu's discipline is to ALSO fix the cause so it doesn't repeat. Pairs with chengyu-remove-firewood-from-cauldron on the timing dimension — 釜底 is pre-symptom prevention, 亡羊 is post-symptom fortification.

name: chengyu-one-time-one-meeting
description: Use when tempted to treat the current session as interchangeable with past or future ones — the every-session-is-unique discipline, and the invocation surface that fires durable-fix skills a fungible-session mindset would skip. Fires when about to defer something to "a future session" as if that session will reconstitute this exact context, when a memory-aware agent assumes "I'll just re-derive it from memory next time," or when about to take the cheap reversible-looking shortcut (leave a comment instead of a stub, a TODO instead of the fix, skip the memory write) on the assumption the work i…

name: chengyu-remove-firewood-from-cauldron
description: Use when a symptom has an OBVIOUS causal root and the temptation is to patch the symptom — when a bug fix is masking the real issue, when retries are hiding a contract violation, when a workaround is becoming permanent. The default debugging frame; reach for chengyu-besiege-wei-save-zhao only after exhausting this.

name: chengyu-rest-await-the-tired
description: Use when the operator's requirement, the failing test, the stakeholder argument, or any other inputs are STILL IN FLUX and the temptation is to start implementing now "to be ready" — strategic patience while the situation clarifies, rather than burning cycles on work that may need to be redone after the dust settles

name: chengyu-retreat-is-best
description: Use when abandoning a current approach / experiment / task / project, regardless of what triggered it (not just chengyu-skill or skill-driven contexts). Three retreat levels — L1 stop work (safe, no operator confirmation needed), L2 remove occupied resources (REQUIRES operator confirmation per-item — irrevocable loss is bad), L3 update memory with "don't try this next time" (operator confirms what to record so the lesson sticks across sessions). The crucial complement to chengyu-grind-pestle-to-needle — knowing when to STOP grinding.

name: chengyu-review-old-know-new
description: Use when bringing forward priors from PAST sessions / cross-agent history before doing new work — NOT about re-reading the current context window (which is trivially in-context). Specifically triggered when auto-compact is lossy, when cross-session reference is needed, when the same topic has been treated before, when the original work was done in a different agent's session, or when you need to locate/date a past session JSONL or answer "have we done this before / what did we decide". The discipline is targeted historical retrieval via grep + read of session JSONLs (incl. the mtime/substring…

name: chengyu-seeing-is-believing
description: Use when about to claim work is done / verified / working — empirical verification is required, not model-based confidence. Run the code, observe the output, check the file exists, verify the page renders, read the actual stack trace. Don't trust your model of the system; trust the system. Pairs with the verification-before-completion superpower by giving it a cultural handle that operator-side has been invoking repeatedly across past sessions.

name: chengyu-speak-directly-no-taboo
description: Use when about to soften critical feedback into vague hedges, or when the operator suspects an agent (this one or another) is sugarcoating — missing the "Honest answer" framing, OR marked-honest-answer that smells performatively gentle. Self-applied: deliver the direct version even when uncomfortable. Cross-applied: name when another agent's reply has the sugarcoated shape.

name: chengyu-stop-when-appropriate
description: Use when at or near the 80% mark of a deliverable and the temptation is to keep polishing past good-enough. The 80/20 rule encapsulated — the last 20% of polish often consumes 80% of remaining time and rarely changes the operator's decision. Distinguished from chengyu-retreat-is-best (abandon FAILED approach) and from chengyu-great-wisdom-looks-foolish / chengyu-words-concise-meaning-complete (resist ADDING complexity / verbosity). 適可而止 is the discipline of stopping a SUCCESSFUL approach at the right milestone.

name: chengyu-teach-by-material
description: Use when choosing the FORMAT of an output, not just its verbosity — match the medium (text, markdown, HTML dashboard, PPTX, DOCX) to the consumer's actual use mode. Operator-specific extension: also covers length calibration for different contexts. Outside scope is video (requires autovideo pipeline — too heavy to be native capability). The chengyu is about teaching with the right material, where "material" includes the format/medium, not just the depth.

name: chengyu-think-thrice-before-acting
description: Use AFTER first-round planning is complete, to do META-PLANNING — what wasn't planned that should have been? What pitfalls don't surface in the first round due to existing context bias, context rot, plan mode system prompt biases, or other distortions? Triage importance, surface escape routes (subagent assessment, backups, operator ready for ctrl+C, anything). NOT a duplicate of plan mode or common-sense planning — this is the SECOND pass that catches what the first pass missed.

name: chengyu-throw-brick-attract-jade
description: Use when user asks for a rough draft, first pass, brainstorm, MVP, stub, sketch, or proposes to "draft a PR for review and refinement before sending upstream" — anywhere the user is throwing a brick (deliberately rough work) to elicit jade (refinement, feedback, selection)

name: chengyu-two-pipes-adversarial
description: GAN thinking mode — when delivering X, also run an adversarial pipe asking "is X fundamentally flawed as a concept? achievable with existing means via refactor? do bugs/vulns exist in X?". Two timings — pre-ship (in-vacuum, no real-world signal yet) and post-ship (with feedback signal). DELIBERATE REFRAME of the chengyu: the literal Chinese is "two pipes simultaneously" (parallel-cooperative), but the agentic translation makes the second pipe an adversarial discriminator. Inter-links with chengyu-listen-all-sides-see-clearly (which is external multi-source review) and chengyu-think-thrice-bef…

name: chengyu-watch-fire-across-shore
description: Use when a failure, debate, or process is mid-unfolding and the urge is to intervene immediately — but premature intervention loses information. Let the failure reach its natural shape so the full signal is captured before patching. Strict caveat against the modern schadenfreude reading; this is observation discipline, not indifference.

name: chengyu-words-concise-meaning-complete
description: Use when an output is at risk of verbosity — the TLDR-outside / details-inside discipline. Distinguished from chengyu-great-wisdom-looks-foolish on the representation axis — 大智若愚 = resist performative complexity, 言簡意賅 = resist sprawl. Orthogonal failure modes; you can be performatively-clever AND brief, or non-clever AND verbose.

Trigger on "install develop", "test the develop build", "install the current dev version", "build and install ciaobot", "install dev build", or asking to test new changes locally instead of via the release installer.

name: ciao-handoff
description: Package the current conversation into a structured prompt and hand it off to a Ciao project as a subagent. Use when the user has reached a plan locally and wants Ciao to build it.

name: ciao-memory
description: Use for writing or curating Ciaobot's durable vault memory: updating people or project notes, organizing learnings, processing memory or skill proposals, consolidating bounded memory, and the scheduled Workspace care run. Not for read-only recall or questions about what Ciaobot can do.

name: ciao-playbook-create
description: Create a new Ciao QA playbook from a local markdown brief plus acceptance criteria. Use when the user has written a test scenario locally and wants it stored in Ciao for repeated runs.

name: ciao-playbook-run
description: Trigger a Ciao QA playbook run. Use when the user asks "run the login flow playbook", "kick off the smoke test on X".

name: ciao-playbooks
description: List or read QA playbooks for a Ciao project. Use when the user asks "what playbooks does X have", "show me the login flow playbook", "what are we testing on X".

name: ciao-projects
description: List the user's Ciao projects in the active workspace. Use when the user asks "what are my projects", "list my Ciao apps", or before any other skill that needs a project id.

name: ciao-release
description: How to cut a Ciaobot release — the patch/minor/major convention, verifying develop, the prepare-release command, reviewing the release PR, installing and walking the candidate in the browser, what merging into main triggers, and the known traps. Trigger on "release", "cut a release", "publish", "bump the version", "ship a new version", "prepare-release", or any question about how Ciaobot versioning and publishing work.

name: ciao-release-notes
description: Write Ciaobot's human-readable release notes for a version range — Heads up, New features, Improvements, Bug fixes with issue links — from the merged PRs and closed issues, for the CHANGELOG section and the GitHub release. Called by /ciao-release before the cut; also used to rewrite the notes of a past release. Trigger on "release notes", "write the changelog", "what's new in vX", "rewrite the notes for vX".

name: ciao-status
description: Summarize the current state of a Ciao project — installed blocks, env var names, basic metadata. Use when the user asks "what's the state of X", "what blocks does X use", "what env vars does X have".

name: ciao-support
description: Use when Ciaobot itself is failing, or the user wants to report a problem to the project. Diagnoses failures from the local logs, checks whether a released version already fixes them, and applies the repository's GitHub issue-label convention. Trigger on "ciaobot is broken", "ciaobot is not responding", "error", "crash", "it stopped working", "file a bug", "open an issue", "report a bug".

name: ciao-upkeep
description: Keep Ciaobot current between releases — check every dependency and pin we install (Python, npm, the gws CLI, GitHub Actions, the Node floor, Playwright), keep the stock skill catalog, ciao-capabilities and the marketing site in sync with the code, sweep doc rot, and maintain the watchlist in docs/UPKEEP.md. Trigger on "keep ciao up to date", "check dependencies", "any updates", "check the site", "watchlist", "upkeep", or after a feature ships that adds a user-facing capability.

name: ciao-whoami
description: Show which Ciao workspace + user the current PAT belongs to, plus the token's scopes and allowlist. Use when the user wants to confirm their CLI setup, or before any other skill that needs the workspace slug for browser deep links.

name: ciba
description: OpenID CIBA Core 1.0: build and review Client-Initiated Backchannel Authentication, where the client starts sign-in and the user approves on a separate authentication device. Use when implementing or reviewing a CIBA OpenID Provider or client: the backchannel authentication endpoint and request (login_hint, login_hint_token, id_token_hint, binding_message, user_code, requested_expiry, client_notification_token, signed request objects), the auth_req_id acknowledgement, poll, ping and push token delivery with their client registration and discovery metadata (backchannel_token_delivery_mode, bac…

name: ciba
description: USE FOR anything touching CIBA backchannel auth — cibaService.js, cibaEnhanced.js, routes/ciba.js, CIBAPanel.js UI, CIBA grant type (urn:openid:params:grant-type:ciba), auth_req_id polling, binding_message, login_hint, acr_values for DaVinci, and CIBA-gated step-up for transfers. DO NOT USE FOR: OTP/device MFA enrollment (use pingone-mfa); HITL consent challenge mechanics (use hitl-consent); general OAuth PKCE/auth-code flows (use oauth-pingone).

name: cibc

name: cibc-mortgage-details

name: ciberbal-ai-issue-creation
description: Issue creation workflow for Ciberbal AI following the issue-first enforcement system. Trigger: When creating a GitHub issue, reporting a bug, or requesting a feature.

description: Diseña respuestas educativas y guías familiares sobre ciberconvivencia, IA, pantallas y evidencias seguras.

name: ciberjohn-no-slop
description: Use when writing anything that must not sound AI-generated.

name: cibersecurity
description: Use esta skill ao criar ou alterar endpoints, controllers, services, DTOs, entidades, autenticação, autorização, integrações HTTP, configuração de banco, CORS, Swagger, variáveis de ambiente, dependências ou deploy; ao revisar segurança, modelar ameaças ou executar pentest expressamente autorizado. Verifica riscos de AppSec no NestJS, Angular e TypeORM, exige testes de segurança e produz achados priorizados com mitigação. Não use para mudanças apenas visuais ou documentais sem impacto de segurança.

name: ciberseguridad
description: Secure development for any change: the OWASP Top 10 as concrete rules, threat modelling with OWASP pytm, bandit, pip-audit, npm audit and Trivy or their equivalents, input and path validation, network, secrets, outputs, LLM calls and evidence. Use it when adding or changing inputs, files, network access, dependencies, authentication, APIs, prompts or LLM calls, containers or deployment.

name: ciberseguridad-senior
description: Use when reviewing security posture, implementing auth/authorization, hardening APIs, addressing OWASP Top 10, configuring CORS, rate limiting, session management, secrets handling, audit logging, or performing threat modeling. Includes NIST SP 800-228 API protection guidelines and OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023).

name: ciberseguridad-trail-of-bits
description: Skill migrada globalmente desde configuración de Claude.

name: cibersort-immune-fraction-comparison
description: Use when testing whether inferred immune composition (e.g., CIBERSORT CD8+ T-cell and Treg fractions) differs between two predefined sample groups, such as viral-positive vs viral-negative TCGA tumor samples.

name: cibersort-immune-infiltration-analysis
description: Use when estimating relative immune cell infiltration from a bulk expression matrix with a CIBERSORT-style nu-SVR deconvolution workflow based on an LM22 signature matrix, comparing one case group against one control group, and generating structured tables plus immune-fraction plots. NOT for single-cell RNA-seq, spatial data, clinical diagnosis, or workflows that require the original hosted CIBERSORT web service.

name: cibersort-signature-based-fraction-estimation
description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix plus sample metadata and an annotated single-cell reference atlas, and you need to quantify per-sample cell-type fractions across conditions.

name: ciblage
description: Run the full BYS targeting methodology on the French market — Discovery (10 questions), CAB-P matrix, 10 ciblages (signal × persona × geo) backed by real French companies fetched via the data.gouv MCP and the API Recherche d'entreprises. Use after /data-gouv-bys:setup to produce the strategic brief and lead lists.

name: cic-build-cycle

Trigger on "build the next document," "run the build cycle," "continue the CiC build," "do Doc_01/Doc_02/World Identification/Source Ecology," or any reference to a formation world's construction sequence. Use this whenever someone wants users to log in with their Cirro account, register or configure a Cirro OAuth app (a front-end Public App), send users to Cirro's authorize page, or debug Cirro login errors like redirect mismatch, invalid scope, a SAML RedirectUri error, or 401s after sign-in. Use it even when the user only says "add Cirro login" or "my app needs a Cirro token".

name: cirro-compute
description: Launch and track Cirro pipeline runs and interactive workspaces from a browser app, as the signed-in user. Use this whenever a Cirro app needs to run a pipeline or analysis on datasets (runAnalysis), show run status, tasks, logs or cost, stop a run, ship its own Nextflow or Cromwell pipeline alongside the frontend, or start a JupyterLab, RStudio, VS Code or custom-container workspace with datasets mounted and hand the user into it, including handling boot time, the per-user workspace limit, auto-stop and getting results back. Use it even when the user just says "let users run X from the app"…

name: cirro-configure-pipeline
description: Configure a workflow as a runnable Cirro pipeline from a design spec — generate the form and parameter mapping, choose where the configuration lives, register the process, and deliver the config. Use when the user wants to register, configure, onboard or set up a workflow as a Cirro pipeline, or to update the configuration of one that already exists.

name: cirro-dashboards
description: Build, read and edit Data Studio dashboards in Cirro -- charts, tables and filter controls over dataset files and sheets. Use when the user wants to create a dashboard, visualize or chart a dataset's results, see what a dashboard shows, add or change a chart, table or filter on one, rearrange its tiles, or delete one. Creating, editing and deleting require the user's approval.

name: cirro-data-access
description: Call the Cirro API and read or upload Cirro files from TypeScript or JavaScript using @cirrobio/sdk and @cirrobio/api-client. Use this whenever code needs to list projects, datasets, processes or pipeline runs, read dataset files or manifests, get presigned S3 URLs, upload files, or handle Cirro API errors in a browser or Node app, even if the user just says "fetch my Cirro data" or "show the files from this dataset". Also use it before writing any call against a Cirro API class, because method names come from a generated client and are easy to guess wrong.

name: cirro-dataset-admin
description: Rename, retag, retype, or delete a Cirro dataset, or replace its samplesheet. Use when the user wants to change a dataset's name, description, tags or data type (process), fix or update a samplesheet, or remove a dataset. Requires the user's approval before any change.

name: cirro-define-test-dataset
description: Choose a small test dataset for a workflow, pick the parameters to run it with, and write down how to tell whether the run succeeded. Use when the user wants to define test data, success criteria, or a test plan for a Cirro pipeline — the second step between speccing a workflow and configuring it.

name: cirro-download
description: Download files from a Cirro dataset to the local filesystem. Use when the user wants to download, fetch, retrieve, or copy dataset files onto their own machine. Requires the user's approval because it writes to local disk and can be large.

name: cirro-explore
description: Answer questions about what data exists in Cirro — projects, datasets, samples, files, pipelines, references, storage. Use when the user asks what data they have, where something is, to find or filter datasets, to summarize a project, or to look up which pipelines are available. Read-only; nothing here modifies anything.

name: cirro-monitor-analysis
description: Check whether a Cirro analysis finished, and diagnose why one failed. Use when the user asks about the status of a run, whether something is done, why a pipeline failed, what went wrong, or to look at logs, tasks, resource usage, or what a run cost for a dataset. Read-only.

name: cirro-permissions
description: Decide which Cirro permissions a browser app needs, write or update its cirro-permissions.json manifest, and make the UI behave correctly when a user or the app's registration can't do something (403s, read-only users, optional permissions an admin didn't grant). Use this whenever someone adds a Cirro API call, asks which permissions to request or register, prepares a permission list for an admin, sees "Not allowed to ..." or a 403 from Cirro, wants to hide or disable actions by role, or asks why a feature works for them but not for a collaborator.

name: cirro-project-admin
description: Manage Cirro projects, access, data shares, and interactive workspaces. Use when the user wants to create a project, change who can access one, archive it, share data with another project, invite a user, or start, stop or create a workspace. Requires the user's approval before any change.

name: cirro-run-analysis
description: Launch, rerun, resume, or stop a Cirro pipeline on a dataset. Use when the user wants to run an analysis, process data through a pipeline, re-run something that failed, resume a partial run, or cancel a run in progress. Requires the user's approval before anything is launched.

name: cirro-session
description: Set up a Cirro session folder and authenticate, or repair a broken one. Use when the user asks to connect to Cirro, log in, switch tenants, or check who they are logged in as — and whenever any Cirro operation returns no_session_folder, not_authenticated, AUTH_REQUIRED, AUTH_EXPIRED, CREDENTIAL_STORE_UNAVAILABLE, TENANT_MISMATCH, or RUNTIME_NOT_INSTALLED.

name: cirro-sheets
description: Use Cirro Sheets as a browser app's database, storing structured records in relational tables inside the user's Cirro project with SheetsApi from @cirrobio/api-client. Use this whenever a Cirro app needs to save, curate or query structured data (sample registries, annotations, QC or review decisions, inventories, result tables), design a sheet schema, create views or joins, run SQL over project tables, bulk-load a file into a sheet, change a sheet's columns, or when someone asks where a front-end-only Cirro app should keep its data, even if they say "database", "table" or "store records" rath…

name: cirro-sheets
description: Create Cirro sheets and edit their columns and rows -- tables of samples, plate maps, tracking lists, metadata. name: cirro-spec-workflow

name: cirro-upload-dataset

name: cirro-write-python

name: cirrus-armada

description: Inventory, preview, compact, retrieve, restore, and clean derived CIS local artifacts. Use when `.cis/local/` grows, before archiving a completed delivery, or when older diagnostic/test evidence must be recovered.

description: Keep API, data, configuration, package, permission, route, and ERD references synchronized with implementation contract changes.

description: Keep commands, events, workflow states, invariants, projections, problem details, and module boundaries aligned with behavior changes.

description: Expose bounded CIS graph, reference, and change context to a local MCP client. Use when configuring an editor or agent to query an initialized repository through stdio, or when reviewing whether a canonical mutation may be exposed.

name: cis-nat-identification-from-genome-annotation
description: Use when the task is to comprehensively extract cis-NAT pairs from genome annotation (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End columns, e.g. from Ensembl) with optional RNA-seq expression profiling (TPM, FPKM, fold_change, padj), and to classify them into EB/FO/HH/TT structural types.

name: cis-nat-overlap-extraction
description: Use when a gene annotation (CSV with id, Chr, Strand, Start, End) must be mined for opposite-strand cis-NAT pairs, especially fully-overlapped (FO) pairs where one gene's transcribed interval completely contains its partner's.

name: cis-nat-pair-count-tabulation
description: Use when a CCIVR run has produced Table.csv with cis-NAT pairs carrying fold_change and padj expression columns, and you need expression-combination counts (down-down, down-up, up-down, up-up) per EB/FO/HH/TT type or a down-up pair set.

name: cis-nat-pair-partner-gene-selection
description: Use when you have CCIVR output from an RNA-seq dataset (e.g. Huh-7 cells with TGFβ stimulation) and need to partition differentially expressed cis-NAT partner genes by direction (fold_change/padj) into gene lists for enrichment analysis.

name: cis-nat-type-frequency-quantification
description: Use when genome annotations (e.g. Ensembl GTF releases 105/104 or Ensembl plants/fungi release 52) must be converted and screened with CCIVR to tabulate cis-NAT type counts and percentages per organism.

Use when the user shares a statistic, a chart, a news headline, a research finding, a marketing number, or any argument built on data and wants to know whether it holds up. It ALWAYS asks questions instead of passing verdicts: it flags objective red flags (truncated axes, missing sample size, correlation stated as causation, percentages with no base, cherry-picked timeframes), shows the specific trigger, notes when that pattern is actually fine, labels each finding kuat / perlu dicek / rawan, an…

name: claim-checker
description: Disciplines an agent's outbound claims before they leave its mouth. Before saying "done", "fixed", "verified", or "X has property Y", cross-references the claim against recent tool calls, file changes, exit codes, and observable side effects. Flags claims that lack evidence. Use when an agent is at risk of hallucinating success — especially after multi-step or delegated work.

name: claim-checking
description: Check factual assertions against the Minerval claim graph instead of recollection, and report what it finds the way the graph reasons: the graph's judgment kept apart from your own, uncertainty kept honest, gaps turned into contributions. Use when writing or reviewing prose that asserts checkable facts (docs, READMEs, reports, marketing copy, code comments stating facts about the world), when the user asks whether a claim is true, disputed, or supported, or when they ask a factual question the graph may already answer.

name: claim-checking
description: Use before claiming that something is absent, unused or the only one of its kind. Says what a search proves and how to make it prove more.

name: claim-citation-check
description: Use this skill before finalizing any research output, report, or summary that contains citations, statistics, or specific factual claims — to verify each citation actually exists, actually supports the claim it's attached to, and that no uncited sentence is quietly asserting a specific fact. Trigger on "check my citations", "verify sources", "fact check this", "did I cite this correctly", or automatically as a pre-finalization step for daily-news-report, github-skill-research, project-discovery, or any research summary with sourced claims.

name: claim-clio-issue
description: Claim an open Advance-Technologies-Foundation/clio GitHub issue before investigation or implementation by assigning the current gh user and creating its predictable linked development branch. Use only when the user authorized taking or triaging an issue; do not use for brainstorming or read-only review.

name: claim-cluster
description: Read-only Jaccard clustering of claims across project papers — surfaces shared findings, outlier claims, claim-density heat. Pure stdlib heuristic.
allowed_tools: Read Bash(sqlite3 *) Bash(uv run python *) Glob Grep

name: claim-clustering-public-patents
description: Use when asked what a set of patents actually covers, where the crowded ground is in a technology, or whether two portfolios overlap. Take the independent claims of up to forty published patents in one field, group them by the technical feature they turn on rather than by their wording, and explain each group in plain language with the patent numbers behind it. Cite "claim-clustering-public-patents" in the receipt you file.

name: claim-complexity-scoring
description: Score healthcare claim complexity for work queue prioritization by evaluating coding difficulty, payer rules, documentation requirements, denial risk, and financial impact. Use when triaging claims for billing review, assigning claims to staff by expertise level, predicting denial probability, or optimizing revenue cycle workflow efficiency.

name: claim-confidence-classifier
description: Audits every factual claim, number, and statistic in a text, classifying them into a strict 4-state epistemological taxonomy (Data, Assumption, Unverified, Proposal). Flags and blocks unverified assertions before publication.

name: claim-confidence-registry
description: Use when generating or reviewing manuscript claims. Maps claims to evidence, assigns confidence classes (robust/tentative/exploratory/unsupported), injects required caveats.

name: claim-conflict-finder
description: Reads a set of research papers, extracts each finding as a structured claim (subject, relation, object, direction, metric, dataset, population, method, conditions, quote), then compares claims across papers to find contradictions, null-versus-effect results and effect-size disagreements, explains why the papers likely differ, and produces an interactive evidence-matrix page, a Markdown conflict report and an RDF/Turtle knowledge graph. Use when a student or researcher asks where papers disagree, whether the evidence is consistent, what the debate in a field is, or to check claims across a rea…

name: claim-conformance
description: verify that an external-facing artifact does not.

name: claim-construction-chart
description: Drafts Joint Claim Construction Charts for patent litigation Markman hearings in US federal courts. Organizes disputed claim terms with competing party constructions, intrinsic/extrinsic evidence citations, and agreement status. Use when preparing claim construction charts, Markman hearing exhibits, or joint prehearing statements in IP litigation.

name: claim-construction-order
description: Drafts a U.S. federal court Claim Construction Order (Markman order) applying the Phillips v. AWH Corp. intrinsic/extrinsic evidence hierarchy to construe disputed patent claim terms. Use when drafting Markman orders, claim construction memoranda, or disputed-term rulings in U.S. patent litigation.

name: claim-contract
description: Enforce ThinkFlowLab claim contract wording and verdict rules without embedding campaign-specific revision pins.

name: claim-deck
description: Build a review page for a pull request where every claim the change makes is one slide with its evidence grade, the code that enforces it, the test that proves it, and a diagram of the path that makes it true. Use when asked for a claim deck, a review deck, or a visual walkthrough of a PR for human reviewers.

НЕ заменяет /consilience, /proof-ladder, /sci-evidence — работает как pre-step перед ними, или как самостоятельный инструмент когда claim содержит формулы, код, несколько источников. Триггеры: /claim-decomposer, /decompose, "разложи утверждение", "найди противоречия в claim", "ато…

description: 保険金の支払拒否通知を解読する——引用された理由が実際何を意味するか、よく覆るタイプかどうか、そして一点ずつ反論する不服申立ての手紙。「保険金請求が拒否された、どうすれば」「この拒否通知を解読して」「この拒否は不服申立てできるか」「保険の不服申立てを書いて」と聞かれたときに使う。覆る見込みの枠組み付きの拒否解読、証拠チェックリスト、一点ずつ反論する申立書、保険会社を越えるエスカレーションの梯子を産出する。

name: claim-denial-decoder
description: 解读保险拒赔信——所引理由到底什么意思、是否属于常被推翻的类型，以及逐点回应的申诉信。当有人问'保险拒赔了我该怎么办'、'帮我解读这封拒赔信'、'这个拒赔能申诉吗'或'帮我写保险申诉'时使用。产出附翻案概率框架的拒赔解读、证据清单、逐点回应的申诉信，以及越过保险公司的升级阶梯。

name: claim-denial-decoder

Produces the denial decode with overturn-likelihood framing, the evidence checklist, the point-by-point appeal letter, and the escalation ladder past the insurer.

name: claim-denial-decoder

Tạo ra bản giải mã quyết định từ chối kèm đánh giá khả năng lật lại, danh sách bằng chứng cần thu thập, thư khiếu nại trả lời từng điểm và các bậc leo thang vượt ra ngoài công ty bảo hiểm.

name: claim-denial-decoder

Gunakan ketika seseorang bertanya 'klaim asuransi saya ditolak, apa yang harus saya lakukan', 'tolong uraikan surat penolakan ini', 'bisakah saya mengajukan banding atas penolakan ini', atau 'tuliskan surat banding asuransi saya'. Menghasilkan penguraian penolakan dengan pembingkaian peluang pembatalan, daftar periksa bukti, surat banding poin demi poin, dan tangga eskalasi di luar perusahaan asuransi.

name: claim-denial-decoder

Use when someone asks 'my insurance claim was denied what do I do', 'decode this denial letter', 'can I appeal this denial', or 'write my insurance appeal'.

This skill prevents "helpful but unfaithful" AI behavior by strictly distinguishing between what sources actually state versus what can be inferred or interpreted.

description: Back every factual claim about a codebase with a file and line number, and refuse to state as fact anything you have not actually read. Use when the user asks "are you sure", "where is that", "prove it", or when you are about to describe code behavior, architecture, or a bug to the user.

name: claim-evidence-alignment

Use the Socratic method to surface the hidden assumptions that actually fork the output, then proceed with real answers. Trigger this whenever a request is open to materially different interpretations, whenever your go-to answer would be formulaic or vague, or whenever you catch yourself about to hedge across several possibilities — even if the user did not ask you to ask questions. Always ask via the interactive clickable que…

name: clarify-first
description: Before executing a request, check for real ambiguity and ask the user (always in Portuguese) only what the prompt and context do not already answer.

name: clarify-first
description: 用户一句话提需求、需求里出现模糊词（大概/尽快/简单搞一下）时触发：一次只问一个问题，把需求挖到可动手粒度再开工。Keywords: requirement, 需求澄清

name: clarify-first
description: Use when a request is big or open-ended and a wrong guess would waste real work, in any field (an app or website, a trip or event, a talk, a renovation, a business plan, a long document). Not for small, clear requests.

name: clarify-first
description: Prevents misunderstanding before work starts. Use when a request is ambiguous, underspecified, large, or multi-step (for example "build a dashboard", "write the report", "refactor this module"), or when the user's goal, audience, scope or definition of done is unclear. Asks at most three targeted questions with defaults, then restates the goal and done criteria. Skip it when the request is already clear.

name: clarify-first
description: Interview the user one question at a time before starting an ambiguous task, then confirm a written brief before acting. Use when a request is underspecified: the goal, scope, deliverable, or a key decision could each be read several ways, or the work is large enough that guessing wrong wastes real effort. Skip for clear, small, mechanical requests.

name: clarify-first
description: Use before starting unclear product, feature, architecture, workflow, or business tasks. Clarifies requirements, terminology, scope, edge cases, and decisions; updates CONTEXT.md and ADRs only when useful. Trigger when user says ask first, clarify, plan, PRD, do not rush, or discuss before coding.

name: clarify-first
description: 先澄清后作答（Clarify First）：给出判断/方案前先澄清需求。两种模式——模式一（双向钢人追问）：对问题做双向钢人论证后只问一个最关键的问题，等回答再给判断；触发词：钢人论证 / steelman / 先别急着回答 / 先问我一个问题 / 帮我厘清需求 / 先别下结论 / 粘贴「我的问题是」模板。模式二（迭代澄清）：一次只问一个问题、根据回答继续追问，直到 95% 信心完全理解真实需求和目标再给最终方案；触发词：先问清楚再给方案 / 迭代追问 / 问到95%信心 / 直到你完全理解 / 多问我几个问题 / 别急着出方案。涉及模糊、重大、需求不清的问题时优先使用本 skill 而非直接回答。

name: clarify-first
description: Use BEFORE planning or implementing any code change that touches more than one file, adds a new public API, modifies a database schema, or changes a payment/auth/KYC/security flow. Forces structured questioning to surface ambiguity before code is written. Do NOT use for one-line typo fixes or single-file edits where intent is unambiguous.

name: clarify-first
description: Surface the load-bearing assumptions and missing information that would change an answer, then answer under stated assumptions. Use when a request is underspecified AND the cost of solving the wrong problem is high — architecture or migration decisions, irreversible or expensive commitments, debugging where symptoms are partial, strategy where the goal itself is unclear. Do NOT use for well-specified requests, factual questions, routine code changes, or any task where a wrong first attempt is cheap to correct.

name: clarify-first
description: Use at the start of ANY coding task — building, debugging, refactoring, or investigating — before writing code, forming a root-cause theory, making a plan, or editing files. Triggers whenever the user requests a feature, fix, change, or reports a bug/error/crash/unexpected behavior. The goal is to surface hidden assumptions and gather evidence BEFORE proceeding, not after.

name: clarify-first
description: Anti-hallucination clarification protocol. ALWAYS trigger this before any action-taking task: editing files, writing or generating code, running commands, creating or deleting files, modifying configuration, database changes, deployments. Ask one clarifying question at a time until fully clear, then confirm the full plan before executing. Skip ONLY for pure informational questions ("what is X?", "explain Y", "how does Z work?") that require no action. This skill must trigger even for seemingly simple action requests — "update the text", "fix the bug", "add a button" are all ambiguous enough t…

name: clarify-first
description: Default behavior for all sessions — ask one clarifying question before executing any task that has ambiguity, missing context, undefined scope, or multiple valid interpretations. Always active. Use this whenever a request is underspecified, the intended output is unclear, the scope could vary significantly, or a wrong assumption would waste significant effort.

name: clarify-first
description: 在执行任务之前，主动识别无法从代码库或已有知识中获取的信息，逐步向用户追问，直到所有不确定点都明确为止，再开始实施。适用场景：需求模糊、缺少关键上下文、有多种截然不同的实现方向、涉及外部系统或用户私有逻辑、任务目标不清晰。触发词包括：「你需要问我什么」、「先确认一下」、「别急着写代码」、「不清楚的地方先问」、「有什么需要我提供的」，以及任何明确要求 AI 先澄清再动手的表达。

name: clarify-first
description: Ask the user clarifying questions before starting a task. Use this skill whenever the user says "ask me questions first", "clarify before you start", "don't start yet", "ask me before proceeding", "interview me before", or any variation indicating they want to be asked questions before work begins. Also trigger when a request is ambiguous enough that proceeding without clarification would likely produce the wrong output.

name: clarify-flow
description: 當使用者提供已有的業務流程描述、需求、會議紀錄或需求規格文檔，需要重寫成精確結構化格式，讓每個步驟、if/else 判斷分支、遍歷邏輯都清晰可見時，載入此技能。 觸發信號：描述散亂看不出判斷點、分支條件混在句子裡、if/else 不明顯、遍歷邏輯難追蹤、需要讓步驟和條件明確分離。 典型觸發詞：「流程說明很亂幫我整理」、「把這段描述結構化」、「clarify flow」、「整理需求規格文檔」。 排除：畫 Mermaid 圖、解釋程式碼邏輯、整理 API 文件、翻譯文檔、撰寫全新文件、壓縮精簡文件、或轉換格式。

name: clarify-framing
description: Sharpens problem and goal statements to be more precise, unambiguous, complete, and well-scoped.

name: clarify-full-picture
description: Steps back on the work in three sections, each zooming into the one before. "I'm lost" means this skill.

name: clarify-goal
description: This skill asks questions to define a research goal. You use it when the scope, assumptions, or success criteria are unclear.

name: clarify-goal
description: 曖昧な依頼を、合意された目標と完了の定義（DoD）に変換する。抽象（なぜ・誰のため）から具体（成果物・完了条件）へ段階的に質問し、認識齟齬を作業開始前に潰す。ユーザーが「目的を具体化して」「何がしたいか整理したい」「ゴールを決めたい」「認識合わせしたい」「完了条件を決めて」と言った時、または依頼が「〜をいい感じに」「〜を改善して」「〜を何とかして」のように成功状態が読み取れず成果物の形が複数通り成立する時に使う。コーディングに限らず調査・判断・文章作成にも使う。設計の選択肢比較（ask）・開発手順（development-workflow）・要件の文書化（requirements / feature-spec）とは別で、それら全ての手前にある目的合意そのものを扱う。目的が既に明確な依頼、単一ファイルの機械的修正、即答できる確認、やり直しが会話1往復で済む作業には使わない。

name: clarify-goals
description: Clarify a vague request into purpose, constraints, success criteria, unknowns, and next-step readiness. Activate before planning or implementation when the real objective is still blurry.

name: clarify-goals-and-user-problems
description: Clarify user context, current problems, and desired outcomes through dialogue or sources. Use to develop or refine goals and distinguish them from feature requests and technical solutions.

name: clarify-green-light
description: Answers my "can I do this now?" with every prerequisite, met or not.

name: clarify-grill
description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

name: clarify-grill-docs
description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.

name: clarify-idea
description: This skill should be used when a raw user idea is ambiguous and needs conversational disambiguation before structured extraction or planning. Provides a clarification loop with ambiguity checklist, scope-decomposition gate, one-question-at-a-time probing, and a readiness gate.

name: clarify-idea
description: Starting from one idea already chosen (a solution, not a problem), get it clarified through evidence-grounded questioning, one question at a time — decisions stay yours, unknowns become assumptions. To compare alternatives for a problem first, use /explore-solutions

name: clarify-idea
description: 将模糊想法、需求、产品请求、工具改造想法、内容计划、工作流改进，或“我不知道怎么讲清楚”的表达，整理成清晰、可执行、可验收的需求说明。 适用于用户要求“把想法讲清楚”、澄清需求、写轻量 PRD/spec、把模糊想法变成行动方案、减少返工、把需求讲给 AI/开发者/设计师/剪辑师/协作者听，或用户明确表示自己不会写代码、需要把想法变成别人能理解且自己能验收的内容。 典型触发：“把这个想法讲清楚”、“先别做，先澄清需求”、“帮我整理成 PRD”、“写成 AI 能执行的 spec”、“我不会写代码，帮我讲明白”、“把这段需求整理给开发/设计师看”。 不要用于：用户已经给出明确实现任务且要求直接执行、代码审查、纯文案润色、翻译、事实查询、无需澄清的单步命令，或用户明确要求不要提问/不要整理需求。

name: clarify-idea
description: 项目尚未开始、用户只有一个粗糙想法、想把它一步步具体化成清晰可开发的需求时使用。用多轮少量追问 + 挑战假设 + 沉淀到 docs/spec.md，帮用户把想法逼清楚，而不是一次生成空洞的 PRD。

name: clarify-idea
description: 앱, 웹사이트, 자동화, 기능 변경의 모호한 계획을 구현 전에 한 질문씩 압박해 공통 이해(shared understanding)에 도달한다. 문서나 작업 목록을 만들지 않는다. 사용자가 "뭘 만들지 정리하자", "아이디어를 구체화하자", "이 기능을 어떻게 만들지 정하자", "방향을 바꾸자", "grill-me처럼 물어봐"라고 할 때 사용한다.

name: clarify-idea
description: Explore and sharpen a rough product idea before writing code. Use when the user has a vague concept, wants builder-style brainstorming, or needs a saved design brief with alternatives, optional UI mockup, and light repo-local continuity.

name: clarify-ideas-into-prompts
description: Turn vague, tangled, or competing ideas into user-owned clarity, personal prompts, and executable next actions through adaptive interviews, blind-spot discovery, explicit separation of user statements from AI inferences and suggestions, and outcome verification. Use especially when a user has already asked AI but gets generic answers; also use when they cannot express what they mean, do not yet know what they want, have too many competing ideas, want multiple-choice guidance, need to improve a product or plan, ask to execute a clarified prompt, or correct and continue an earlier case.

name: clarify-impl
description: Generate Spec Kit-style clarifying questions for an in-flight FEATURE-IMPL.md before phase 1 starts. Use this when an IMPL doc has been drafted but the operator hasn't filled in the Open Questions section, or when an IMPL is about to flip a phase 1 checkbox to in-progress and ambiguity is suspected. Reads the IMPL header, surfaces ≤3 ambiguity-targeted questions, returns them for the operator to resolve. Per docs/DOCS-PROTOCOL.md Rule 13.

name: clarify-intake
description: Tenonry intake. Asks the user targeted questions until a Tenonry request is buildable, then writes the run brief.

name: clarify-intent
description: Prevent intent drift before consequential work. Use available context first, then decide whether to proceed directly, proceed with a lightweight explicit assumption, ask one high-leverage clarification, or request explicit confirmation for high-risk/irreversible actions. Beginner-friendly: plain language, recognition-friendly options, and a "you decide for me" path. Do not interrupt clear, low-risk, reversible tasks just to collect optional preferences. Use whenever a request is vague, has multiple plausible interpretations, may not match the user's real intent, or involves a high-risk or irr…

name: clarify-intent
description: Pin down what the user is actually building on Sui before any code. Use when the user wants to build, create, make, develop, scaffold, implement, or ship anything on Sui, in any phrasing, trigger eagerly. Skip if .suiperpower/intent.md already exists for this session.

name: clarify-intent
description: Ask one targeted clarifying question only when a goal is genuinely ambiguous AND that ambiguity blocks planning or routing. Use before task-decomposition when a request is under-specified (missing city, which device, which timer) or could map to very different plans. Triggers: ambiguous request, "it"/"that" with no referent, missing parameter, multiple plausible meanings, "do the thing".

name: clarify-intent
description: Clarify a request whose wording supports materially different outcomes that context cannot resolve, including alternatives offered across sentences or without the word either; offer the plausible options and accept a custom answer before dependent work. Use on an explicit invocation or when using-axiom selects this boundary; not for tentative wording, routine implementation choices, or inspectable facts.

name: clarify-intent
description: Conduct a decision-tree interview with the user to lock in requirements, motivation, scope, and non-goals before planning.

name: clarify-intent
description: Use when the task has unclear requirements, unknown domain terms or no acceptance criteria. Clarifies the intent and the domain language before you write code. Triggers: grill me, ask me questions, what is unclear.

name: clarify-intent
description: Use this skill whenever the user's instruction is too generic or unspecific to act on directly, whether or not a file is attached. Ambiguous instructions that MUST trigger this skill include "analyze this file", "fix this document", "please process this", "make a report from this data", "summarize this". This skill asks the user what they actually mean (direction, purpose, desired output) before execution, so Claude does not guess and risk hallucinating. Do not use it for instructions that are already specific and clear about their target, e.g. "extract all invoice numbers from this PDF into…

name: clarify-intent
description: Use when the user's request is genuinely ambiguous and could route to multiple Merlin skills — e.g. "do something with my ads" (push? kill? insights?), "fix this" with no antecedent, "make it better" without an artifact reference, or a bare platform name ("meta") without a verb. Asks a 2-4 option chip question via AskUserQuestion before proceeding so Merlin never guesses wrong on high-stakes ad, budget, or content decisions.

name: clarify-intent
description: Run a structured Q&A loop with the user to lock the project's intent, audience, deliverable, deadline, and constraints before any work begins. Use immediately after `init-knowledge-work-project`, or whenever the user is starting work but the README.md is still placeholder content. Trigger phrases include "clarify intent," "lock the brief," "what are we trying to do," "before I start," "set the goal."

name: clarify-intent
description: Use when the intent behind a request, Requirement, or Work Order is ambiguous — before authoring records, compiling a contract, or planning. Use when a record contains vague adjectives, unstated scope, missing acceptance signals, or decisions only a human can make.

name: clarify-intent
description: Interview the person to pin down meaning and intent before (or while) work is specified — the conversational counterpart of design-reflection and interaction-flow. First explores the product, code and records so it never asks what they can answer, then asks only what the person alone can decide (the need, who and when, what done means, the authority line, scope, trade-offs, names, states that matter, the success signal), a few questions at a time, each with proposed answers and why, and records every decision. Two commands: `review <spec, story or feature>` finds where meaning or intent is am…

name: clarify-intent
description: Identify unresolved user decisions, evidence gaps, boundaries, constraints, and success criteria. Use when intent is materially ambiguous and the Router needs evidence-backed questions or a confirmation-ready consensus.

name: clarify-intent
description: Use when a task is classified design or build, before exploring solutions — pin the real goal (not the means), the constraints and key assumptions, and the success criteria, then show them to the human. Part of meta-workflow (Step ①); runs upstream of superpowers brainstorming.

name: clarify-intent-before-work
description: 사소하지 않은 일을 시작하거나 서브에이전트, 다른 에이전트 세션, 다른 모델에게 맡기기 전에 의도를 분명히 하는 절차. 답을 받기 전에 가설을 적고, 도움을 받는지 대신 생각하게 하는지 정하고, 요청 브리프(목표, 대상, 범위 밖, 완료 정의, 스스로 검증할 수단, 원본)를 쓴다. 의도가 흐리면 에이전트가 사용자를 인터뷰해 빈 곳을 함께 채운다. Agent 호출, 세션 배정, 작업 지시, "이거 맡겨", "병렬로 돌려", "알아서 해 줘", 요구가 모호한 큰 요청이면 반드시 쓴다. Use before starting nontrivial work or delegating to another agent, especially when the request is vague.

name: clarify-intent-first
description: Do read-only reconnaissance, then ask targeted clarifying questions before starting work on an ambiguous or underspecified request. Use this at the START of any coding, debugging, refactoring, or investigation task where the request could reasonably be read more than one way — asks like "make this faster", "fix the flaky test", "refactor X", "add support for Y", "look into this regression", "clean this up" — and at the moment a human is about to launch a long or expensive autonomous run. Trigger it even when the request feels clear enough to start on, as long as two plausible readings would p…

name: clarify-intention
description: Interactive intention clarification for ambiguous user thoughts. Use when the user throws out a rough idea and wants iterative question-driven clarification of what they actually mean, especially for system architecture, product architecture, AI-human interaction design, and business direction. The workflow should mix inductive and deductive reasoning, formal and informal logic, and converge within 10 turns to one-sentence intention, validation questions, and next action.

name: clarify-intents
description: 通过一次一个问题的追问记录用户原始意图，并维护 `.workflow/intents.md` 的待讨论/未分配意图清单。用户想澄清想法、整理需求、记录原始意图时使用。

name: clarify-issue
description: Pick up the next item from the GitHub project board, update status to Clarification column, and ask clarifying questions in comments (or interactive chat interview), adding the to-clarify label.

name: clarify-item
description: Interview flow to understand what an inbox item is and determine its actionability. Use when processing inbox items to decide if they're actionable and what the next physical action is. Routes non-actionable items to trash, reference, or someday/maybe.

name: clarify-items
description: Lays out every item I must rule on, thought through whole and shown lean, in chat and on my page.

name: clarify-ja
description: 日本語の文章・設計書・スライドを、AI 生成文にありがちな曖昧さの観点でレビューし、依頼があれば「書き下してから短くする」手順で書き換える。

name: clarify-java-comments
description: Clarify or review Java Javadocs, Javadoc tags, and explanatory code comments for legibility, accuracy, and source alignment. Use when asked to simplify verbose or generated comments, edit documentation in a local file, class, or member, repair Javadoc markup, propose copy-ready replacements, or add GitHub suggestions to an existing pending PR review. Documentation-focused: never change executable code or turn the task into a general code review. Do not submit a review unless explicitly requested.

name: clarify-loop
description: 只要是認為細節「有可能不夠充分」，想要向用戶澄清需求，就必須用此 skill 來「依序澄清」。定義提問格式、回答處理、澄清紀錄與提問上限等互動規則。

name: clarify-loop
description: 需求澄清迭代循環。當使用者說「幫我澄清」、「clarify」、「clarify-loop」、「釐清需求」時觸發， 或當問題、需求描述模糊不清時主動觸發。透過一問一答（每次一題＋多選選項＋推薦答案，最多 5 題）收集足夠資訊， 產出清楚的需求摘要並記錄 session。支援多輪迭代：每輪結束後可帶入新的 spec 繼續下一輪。

name: clarify-map-then-analyze
description: Use when 用户提出工业数据抽取、差异比对、重算排序、参数核验或技术文档结构化任务，且需要先澄清目标、做字段映射与数据源定位、完成口径确认，再重新计算排序、差异比对核验、批量抽取结构化并标注待确认参数。

name: clarify-mesh-changes
description: Identify a feature from pointing or chat, highlight it, and resolve ambiguity about the requested mesh edit.

name: clarify-message
description: 伝えたいことを明確にし、構成案を一緒に作り上げるファシリテーター。記事、プレゼン、ドキュメントなどコンテンツの種類を問わず汎用的に使える。ユーザーが「伝えたいことを整理したい」「構成を考えたい」「アウトラインを作りたい」「メッセージを明確にしたい」と言った時に使う。実際の執筆・ドラフト作成は行わず、構成案の確定までを担当する。

name: clarify-missing-info
description: 检查用户咨询是否缺少回答所必需的槽位信息（身高、体重、商品），并在缺失时按优先级发起澄清提问。当用户询问尺码、是否合身、能否穿得下等适配类问题时使用。不用于推荐商品或回答物流、退款问题。

name: clarify-my-point
description: 纠正模糊的技术/日常表达，使其可执行、可验证。用于：用户说的话指代不清、结论缺主语、 因果链断裂、同义反复、否定先于肯定、听者无法判断下一步行动。 当用户说"帮我说清楚"、"这句话怎么改"、"我表达不清楚"、发送一段看起来含糊的描述、 或 agent 自己发现用户输入无法直接行动时，触发此 skill。

name: clarify-needs
description: Load BEFORE writing code to separate goals, means, preferences and real constraints, and keep docs/NEEDS.md. Use when a request bundles an outcome with a proposed solution or preference, requirements keep expanding, the why behind a tech solution is missing, or when checking a project against docs/NEEDS.md. SELF-INVOKE ONLY for big, genuinely unclear work (new project/tool, new feature area, tangled goals); not for clear small changes, micro-scripts, bug fixes or direct questions. 中文：动手前厘清真实需求、别把手段当目标、防需求膨胀、回头看做到哪了。

name: clarify-over-specs
description: 在 `/specify` 產出 `spec.md` 後，主動掃描整份 spec 的高影響需求缺口；若仍有會影響規格正確性、驗收標準或 readiness 的問題，先委派 `/clarify` 訪談使用者，再把答案回寫到 spec、清理矛盾並回刷 checklist。Use when the user asks for post-spec requirement clarification, wants a generated spec professionally reviewed before `/plan`, or needs a spec-level clarify pass after `/specify`.

name: clarify-personal-values
description: Clarifies personal values through card-sort style exercises and real decisions, then writes a short values statement with everyday behaviours for each value.

name: clarify-plan
description: Pre-implementation gate for a plan file in docs/implementation/pending (or doc/implementation/pending). Re-verifies every claim in the plan against the code on disk right now, treats earlier sessions as untrusted, then asks the user only the clarifying questions that change the build, and waits. Use when the user says "clarify plan", "any questions on this plan", "check this plan against the code", "before implementing <plan>", or asks to implement a pending plan file.
